items.title: Institutional Regulations on Master Authority, Slave Earnings & Slander Penalties
items.description: Prophetic legislation regulating master-slave relations: forbidding masters from appropriating female slave prostitution earnings (kasb al-ima'), establishing master maintenance duties, and legislating punishment in the hereafter for masters who falsely accuse their slaves.

hadiths.english_text: Narrated 'Abdullah bin Zama: That he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) delivering a sermon, and he mentioned the she-camel and the one who hamstrung it. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) recited:-- 'When, the most wicked man among them went forth (to hamstrung the she-camel).' (91.12.) Then he said, "A tough man whose equal was rare and who enjoyed the protection of his people, like Abi Zama went forth to (hamstrung) it." The Prophet (ﷺ) then mentioned about the women (in his sermon). "**It is not wise for anyone of you to lash his wife like a slave, for he might sleep with her the same evening.**" Then he advised them not to laugh when somebody breaks wind and said, "Why should anybody laugh at what he himself does?"

Narrated Abu Burda's father: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "**any man who has a slave girl whom he educates properly, teaches good manners, manumits and marries her, will get a double reward** And if any man of the people of the Scriptures believes in his own prophet and then believes in me too, he will (also) get a double reward **And any slave who fulfills his duty to his master and to his Lord, will (also) get a double reward**"

Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Umar: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Everyone of you is a guardian and everyone of you is responsible (for his wards). A ruler is a guardian and is responsible(for his subjects); a man is a guardian of his family and responsible (for them); a wife is a guardian of her husband's house and she is responsible (for it), **a slave is a guardian of his master's property and is responsible (for that)**. Beware! All of you are guardians and are responsible (for your wards)."
Narrated Abu Huraira: **The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade taking the earnings of a slave girl by prostitution**

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The best alms is that which is given when one is rich, and a giving hand is better than a taking one, and you should start first to support your dependents." A wife says, 'You should either provide me with food or divorce me.' **A slave says, 'Give me food and enjoy my service.'** A son says, "Give me food; to whom do you leave me?" The people said, "O Abu Huraira! Did you hear that from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" He said, "No, it is from my own self."

Narrated Abu Huraira: I heard Abu-l-Qasim (the Prophet) saying, "**If somebody slanders his slave and the slave is free from what he says, he will be flogged on the Day of Resurrection unless the slave is really as he has described him.**"

items.title: The Barirah Precedents: Patronage (Wala') Vests Exclusively in the Purchaser / Dissolution of Enslaved Marriage
items.description: A massive body of canonical hadiths establishing key pillars of Islamic slave jurisprudence: (1) Patronage and inheritance rights (wala') belong exclusively to the one who pays the purchase price and manumits (al-walā' liman a'taq); (2) When an enslaved woman married to an enslaved man is emancipated, she receives the unilateral right (khiyār al-'itq) to dissolve her marriage because her husband remains a slave; (3) Charity received by a slave transforms into lawful gifts when passed to free masters.

hadiths.english_text: Narrated 'Aishah (ra) that **Barira came to seek her help in writing of emancipation and she had to pay five Uqiya (of gold) by five yearly installments.** 'Aishah said to her, **"Do you think that if I pay the whole sum at once, your masters will sell you to me, and I will free you and your Wala' will be for me."** Barira went to her masters and told them about that offer. They said that **they would not agree to it unless her Wala' would be for them.** 'Aishah further said, "I went to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and told him about it." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to her, **"Buy Barira and manumit her and the Wala' will be for the liberator."** Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then got up and said, **"What about those people who stipulate conditions that are not present in Allah's Laws? If anybody stipulates a condition which is not in Allah's Laws, then what he stipulates is invalid. Allah's Condition (Laws) are the truth and are more solid."**

Narrated 'Urwa: That 'Aisha told him that **Barirah came to seek her help in her writing of emancipation (for a certain sum) and that time she had not paid anything of it.** 'Aisha said to her, **"Go back to your masters, and if they agree that I will pay the amount of your writing of emancipation and get your Wala', I will do so."** Barirah informed her masters of that but they refused and said, **"If she (i.e. 'Aisha) is seeking Allah's reward, then she can do so, but your Wala' will be for us."** 'Aisha mentioned that to Allah's Apostle who said to her, **"Buy and manumit (free) her, as the Wala' is for the liberator."** Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then got up and said, **"What about the people who stipulate conditions which are not present in Allah's Laws? Whoever imposes conditions which are not present in Allah's Laws, then those conditions will be invalid, even if he imposed these conditions a hundred times. Allah's conditions (Laws) are the truth and are more solid."**

Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Umar: **Aisha wanted to buy a slave-girl in order to manumit her. The girl's masters stipulated that her Wala' would be for them.** Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said (to 'Aisha), **"What they stipulate should not stop you, for the Wala' is for the liberator."**

Narrated Aisha: Barirah came (to 'Aisha) and said, **"I have made a contract of emancipation with my masters for nine Uqiyas (of gold) to be paid in yearly installments. Therefore, I seek your help."** 'Aisha said, **"If your masters agree, I will pay them the sum at once and free you on condition that your Wala' will be for me."** Barirah went to her masters but they refused that offer. She (came back) and said, **"I presented to them the offer but they refused, unless the Wala' was for them."** Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) heard of that and asked me about it, and I told him about it. On that he said, **"Buy and manumit her and stipulate that the Wala' should be for you, as Wala' is for the liberator."** 'Aisha added, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then got up amongst the people, Glorified and Praised Allah, and said,"Then after: **What about some people who impose conditions which are not present in Allah"s Laws? So, any condition which is not present in Allah's Laws is invalid even if they were one-hundred conditions. Allah's ordinance is the truth, and Allah's condition is stronger and more solid. Why do some men from you say, O so-and-so! manumit the slave but the Wala will be for me? Verily, the Wala is for the liberator."**

Narrated 'Amra bint 'Abdur-Rahman: **Barirah went to Aisha, the mother of the faithful believers to seek her help in her emancipation Aisha said to her, "If your masters agree, I will pay them your price in a lump sum and manumit (free) you."** Barirah mentioned that offer to her masters but **they refused to sell her unless the Wala' was for them.** 'Aisha told Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) about it. He said, **"Buy and manumit her as the Wala' is for the liberator."**

Narrated 'Urwa: Aisha told me that **Barirah came to seek her help in writing for emancipation and at that time she had not paid any part of her price.** 'Aisha said to her, **"Go to your masters and if they agree that I will pay your price (and free you) on condition that your Wala' will be for me, I will pay the money."** Barirah told her masters about that, but they refused, and said, **"If 'Aisha wants to do a favor she could, but your Wala will be for us."** Aisha informed Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) of that and he said to her, **"Buy and manumit Barirah as the Wala' will go to the manumitted."**

Narrated 'Urwa:Aisha said, **"Barirah came to me and said,"My people (masters) have written the contract for my emancipation for nine Awaq ) of gold) to be paid in yearly installments, one Uqiyya per year; so help me."**Aisha said (to her),**"If your masters agree, I will pay them the whole sum provided the Wala will be for me."**Barirah went to her masters and told them about it, but they refused the offer and she returned from them while Allah"s Messenger (ﷺ) was sitting. She said, **"I presented the offer to them, but they refused unless the Wala' would be for them."** When the Prophet (ﷺ) heard that and 'Aisha told him about It, he said to her, **"Buy Barirah and let them stipulate that her Wala' will be for them, as the Wala' is for the manumitted."** 'Aisha did so. After that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) got up amidst the people, Glorified and Praised Allah and said, **"What is wrong with some people who stipulate things which are not in Allah's Laws? Any condition which is not in Allah's Laws is invalid even if there were a hundred such conditions. Allah's Rules are the most valid and Allah's Conditions are the most solid. The Wala is for the manumitted."**

Narrated 'Amra: Aisha said that **Barirah came to seek her help in the writing of her emancipation.** 'Aisha said to her, **"If you wish, I will pay your masters (your price) and the wala' will be for me."** When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came, she told him about it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to her, **"Buy her (i.e. Barirah) and manumit (free) her, for the Wala is for the one who manumits."** Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit and said, **"What about those people who stipulate conditions which are not in Allah's Laws? Whoever stipulates such conditions as are not in Allah's Laws, then those conditions are invalid even if he stipulated a hundred such conditions."**

Narrated 'Aisha: **Three principles were established because of Barira: (i) When Banra was manumitted she was given the option (to remain with her slave husband or not). (ii) Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said "The Wala of the slave) is for the one who manumits (the slave).** (iii) When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) entered (the house), he saw a cooking pot on the fire but he was given bread and meat soup from the soup of the home. The Prophet (ﷺ) said,"Didn't I see the cooking pot (on the fire)?"It was said,"That is the meat given in charity to Barira, and you do not eat the (things given in) charity."The Prophet (ﷺ) said,**"It is an object of charity for Barira, and it is a present for us**

Narrated 'Aisha: (the wife of the Prophet) **Three traditions were established concerning situations in which Barra was involved: When she was manumitted, she was given the option to keep her husband or leave him; Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "The wala is for the one who manumits,** Once Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) entered the house while some meat was being cooked in a pot, but only bread and some soup of the house were placed before, him. He said,"Don't I see the pot containing meat?"They said,"Yes, but that meat was given to Barira in charity (by someone), and you do not eat what it given in charity."The Prophet (ﷺ) said**"That meat is alms for her, but for us it is a present**

Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: **Barira's husband was a slave called Mughith, as if I am seeing him now, going behind Barira and weeping with his tears flowing down his beard.** The Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Abbas, **"O 'Abbas ! are you not astonished at the love of Mughith for Barira and the hatred of Barira for Mughith?"** The Prophet (ﷺ) then said to Barira, **"Why don't you return to him?"** She said, **"O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Do you order me to do so?"** He said, **"No, I only intercede for him."** She said, **"I am not in need of him."**

Narrated Al-Aswad: **Aisha intended to buy Barira, but her masters stipulated that her wala wound be for them.** Aisha mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ) who said (to 'Aisha), **"Buy and manumit her, for the wala is for the one who manumits."** Once some meat was brought to the Prophet (ﷺ) and was said, "This meat was given in charity to Barira." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, **"It is an object of charity for Barira and a gift for us."** Narrated Adam: Shu'ba related the same Hadith and added: **Barira was given the option regarding her husband**

Narrated Qasim bin Muhammad: **Three traditions have been established because of Barira: "Aisha intended to buy her and set her free, but Barira"s masters said, "Her wala' will be for us."** 'Aisha mentioned that to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) who said, **"You could accept their condition if you wished, for the wala is for the one who manumits the slave." Barira was manumitted, then she was given the choice either to stay with her husband or leave him;** One day Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) entered 'Aisha's house while there was a cooking pot of food boiling on the fire. The Prophet (ﷺ) asked for lunch, and he was presented with bread and some extra food from the home-made Udm (e.g. soup). He asked, "Don't I see meat (being cooked)?" They said, "Yes, O Allah's Apostle! But it is the meat that has been given to Barira in charity and she has given it to us as a present." He said, **"For Barira it is alms, but for us it is a present."**

Narrated 'Aisha: that **she intended to buy Barira (a slave girl) and her masters stipulated that they would have her Wala'.** When 'Aisha mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ) ; he said, **"Buy her, for the Wala' is for the one who manumits."**

Narrated 'Aisha: **I bought Barira (a female slave).** The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to me), **"Buy her as the Wala' is for the manumitted."** Once she was given a sheep (in charity). The Prophet (ﷺ) said, **"It (the sheep) is a charitable gift for her (Barira) and a gift for us."** Al-Hakam said, "Barira's husband was a free man." Ibn 'Abbas said, **'When I saw him, he was a slave**

Narrated Al-Aswad: **'Aisha bought Barira in order to manumit her, but her masters stipulated that her Wala' (after her death) would be for them.** 'Aisha said, **"O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! I have bought Barira in order to manumit her, but her masters stipulated that her Wala' will be for them."** The Prophet (ﷺ) said, **"Manumit her as the Wala is for the one who manumits (the slave)," or said, "The one who pays her price."** Then 'Aisha bought and manumitted her. **After that, Barira was given the choice (by the Prophet) (to stay with her husband or leave him). She said, "If he gave me so much and so much (money) I would not stay with him."** (Al-Aswad added: Her husband was a free man.) The sub-narrator added: The series of the narrators of Al-Aswad's statement is incomplete. The statement of Ibn 'Abbas, i.e., **when I saw him he was a slave**, is more authentic
Narrated Ibn 'Umar: **The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the selling of the Wala' (of slaves) or giving it as a present**

Narrated Ibn 'Umar: That **Aisha, the mother of the Believers, intended to buy a slave girl in order to manumit her. The slave girl's master said, "We are ready to sell her to you on the condition that her Wala should be for us."** Aisha mentioned that to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) who said, **"This (condition) should not prevent you from buying her, for the Wala is for the one who manumits (the slave)."**

Narrated Al-Aswad:Aisha said, **"I bought Barira and her masters stipulated that the Wala would be for them."** Aisha mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he said, **"Manumit her, as the Wala is for the one who gives the silver (i.e. pays the price for freeing the slave)."** Aisha added, **"So I manumitted her. After that, the Prophet caller her (Barira) and gave her the choice to go back to her husband or not. She said,"If he gave me so much and so much (money) I would not stay with him."So she selected her ownself (i.e. refused to go back to her husband)."**

Narrated Ibn 'Umar: When Aisha intended to buy Barira, she said to the Prophet, **"Barira's masters stipulated that they will have the Wala."** The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to Aisha), **"Buy her, as the Wala is for the one who manumits."**
Narrated Aisha: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, **"The wala is for the one who gives the silver (pays the price) and does the favor (of manumission after paying the price)."**

Anas b. Malik reported that Barira presented to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a piece of meat which had been given to her as sadaqa. Upon this he (ﷺ) said:**"That is a Sadaqa for her and a gift for us."**

A'isha reported that (once) the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon him, ) was presented with beef. It was said (by someone) that it had been given to Barira as Sadaqa. Upon this he (the Prophet) said:**"It is a Sadaqa for her and a gift for us."**

A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) said: **Three are the decions (of the Shari'ah that we have come to know) through Barira.** The people gave her sadaqa and she offered us as gift. We made a mention of it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whereupon he said: **"It is a sadaqa for her and a gift for you; so eat it."**

Ibn Umar reported that **'A'isha decided to buy a slave-girl and then set her free, but her masters said:We are prepared to sell her to you on the condition that her right of inheritance would vest with you.** She (Hadrat A'isha) made a mention of that to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) whereupon he said: **"This should not stand in your way. The right of inheritance vests in one who emancipates."**

A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported that **Barira came to her in order to seek her help in securing freedom, but she had (so far) paid nothing out of that sum stipulated in the contract.** 'A'isba said to her. **Go to your family (who owns you), and if they like that I should pay the amount (of the contract) on your behalf (for purchasing your freedom), then I shall have the right in your inheritance. (If they accepted it) I am prepared (to make this payment).** Barira made a mention of that to the (members of) her family, but they refused and said:**If she (Hadrat 'A'isha) wants to do good to You for the sake of Allah, she may do it, but the right of inheritance will be ours.** She (Hadrat 'A'isha) made a mention of that to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), and he said to her: **Buy her, and emancipate her, for the right of inheritance vests with one who emancipates (the slave).** Allah's Messenger, may peace be upon him) then stood up and said: **"What has happened to the people that they lay down conditions which are not (found) in the Book of Allah? And he who laid down a condition not found in the Book of Allah, that is not valid. even if it is laid down hundred times. The condition laid down by Allah is the most weighty and the most valid."**

A'isha, the wife of Allah's Apostle (ﷺ), reported: Barira came to me and said: **"'A'isha, I have entered into a contract for securing freedom with my family (who owns me) for nine 'uqiyas of silver, one 'uqiya every year."** The rest of the hadith is the same (but with this addition): **"This (the problem of the right of inheritance) should not stand in your way. Buy her, and set her free."** He said in the hadith: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stood up among men, extolled Allah, praised Him, and then said: **"The right of inheritance (Wala') belongs only to the one who emancipates."**

A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported: Barira came to me and said: **"My family (owners) have made a contract with me for granting freedom for nine 'uqiyas of silver payable in nine years, one 'uqiya every year. Help me in making this payment."** I said to her: **"If your family agrees, I will pay them the whole sum at once, provided the right of inheritance (Wala') vests in me."** Barira went to her owners, but they refused unless the right of inheritance remained with them. When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) heard of it, he said: **"Buy her and emancipate her, for the right of inheritance vests only in the one who emancipates."** Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stood on the pulpit and said: **"What is the matter with people that they lay down conditions not in the Book of Allah? Any condition not in the Book of Allah is invalid even if laid down a hundred times. The right of inheritance (Wala') vests only in the one who emancipates."**

Hisham b. 'Urwa narrated a hadith like this with the same chain of trans- mitters except (with this change) that in the hadith transmitted on the authority of jartr (the words are):**Her (Barira's) husband was a slave, so Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) gave her the option (either to retain her matrimonial relation with her husband or sever it off). She opted to break off (and secure freedom for her even from the matrimonial alliance). And if he were free he would not have given her the option.** In the hadith narrated on the authority (of this chain of transmitters) these words are not found: Amma ba'du

Abd al-Rahman b. al. Qasim reported on the authority of his father:'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) said: **There were three issues which were clarified in case of Barira: her owners had decided to sell her on the condition that the right of her inheritance would vest with them.** She ('A'isha) said: I made a mention of that to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and he said: **Buy her and emancipate her, for verily the right of inheritance vests with one who emancipates. She said that she emancipated (her) and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) gave her the option (either to retain her matrimonial alliance or break it after emancipation). She (taking advantage of the option) opted for herself (the severing of matrimonial alliance).** 'A'isha said: The people used to give her charity and she gave us that as gift. I made a mention of it to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ), whereupon he said: **"That is charity for her but gift for you, so take that."**

A'isha (Allah's be pleased with her) reported that **she had bought Barira from the people of Ansar, but they laid down the condition that the right of inheritance (would vest in them),** whereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:**The right of inheritance vests with one who shows favour (who emancipates)** and **Allah's Messenger (may peacebe upon him) gave her the choice (either to retain) her matrimonial alliance or break it). Her husband was a slave.** She (Barira also) gave 'A'isha some meat as gift. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: I wish you could prepare (cook) for us out of this meat. 'A'isha said, It has been given as charity to Barira, whereupon he said: **"That is charity for her and gift for us."**

A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported: **She wanted to buy Barira with a view to emancipating her. They (the sellers) laid down the condition that the right of inheritance would vest (with them).** She (Hadrat 'A'isha) made a mention of that to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), whereupon he said: **Buy her and emancipate her for the right of inheritance vests with one who emancipates.** Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was given meat as gift. They (his Companions) said to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ): This was given as charity to Barira, whereupon he said: **That is charity for her but gift for us.** And **she was given option (to retain her matrimonial alliance or to break it).** Abd al-Rahman said: Her husband was a free man. Shu'ba said: I then asked him (one of the narrators) about Barira's husband (whether he had been a free mart or a slave), whereupon he said: "I do not know."
A'isha reported that **the husband of Barira was a slave**

A'isha (Allah be pleased with her). the wife of Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said: **Three are the Sunan (usages) (that we came to know in case of Bairara). She was given option in regard to her husband when she was emancipated.** Sbe was given meat as charity. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) visited me when an earthen pot with meat in it was placed on the fire. He asked for food and be was given bread with ordinary meat (usually cooked in the) house. Thereupon he (Allah's Messenger) said: Don't I see the earthen pot on fire with meat in it? They said: Yes. Allah's Messenger, there is meat in it which was given as charity to Barira. We did not deem it advisable that we should give you that to eat, whereupon he said: **It is charity for her, but it is gift for us.** Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) also said: **"The right of inheritance vests with one who emancipates."**

Abu Huraira (Allah be pleased with him) reported: **'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) thought of buying a slave-girl and emancipating her, but her owners refused to (sell her but on the condition) that the right of inheritance would vest in them.** She made a mention of that to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). whereupon he said: **"Let this (condition) not stand in your way for the right of inheritance vests with one who emancipates."**

categories.category_description: Comprehensive primary evidence from the Qur'an establishing the theological and legal foundation of slavery in Islam. Features Arthur Droge's literal English translation alongside classical exegesis from Tafsir al-Tabari and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, documenting the divine sanction of right-hand possession (Milk al-Yamin), sexual cohabitation with married female war captives, master ownership rights, modesty exceptions, and chattel property parables.

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: If you fear that you will not act fairly toward the orphan girls, marry what seems good to you of the women: two, or three, or four. But if you fear that you will not be fair, (marry only) one, or what your right (hands) own. That (will make it) more likely that you will not be biased.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Caps marriage at four free wives, while permitting unlimited slave concubinage without numerical ceiling. Cohabitation with female slaves serves as a legal alternative when fearing injustice, as masters are exempt from equal partition of nights among chattel.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Marrying Only One Wife or Relying on Concubines When Fearing Injustice

Regarding Allah's statement: **{But if you fear that you will not be fair, (marry only) one, or what your right (hands) own}**, **it means: if you fear that you will not be able to do justice between your wives by multiplying women**, as Allah said: **{You will never be able to do perfect justice between wives even if it is your ardent desire}** [4:129]. **So whoever fears that, let him limit himself to one wife, or to female slave concubines, for it is not obligatory to divide time among them, rather it is recommended. So if one does so, that is good, and if not, there is no harm.**

Regarding His statement: **{That (will make it) more likely that you will not be biased}**, some scholars said this means more likely that your dependents do not become numerous. This was stated by Zayd bin Aslam, Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah, and Ash-Shafi'i, derived from Allah's statement: **{And if you fear poverty ('Aylatan)...}** [9:28]. The Arabs say: *'Aal ar-rajulu, ya'ilu, 'aylatan,* when one becomes poor. However, this interpretation is questionable, **because just as a large number of dependents is feared from a multitude of free wives, it is also feared from a multitude of concubines.**

The correct view is the position of the majority regarding **{That (will make it) more likely that you will not be biased}**, **meaning: that you do not do injustice.** It is said: *'Aala* in judgment when one deviates, oppresses, and acts unjustly. Abu Talib recited in his famous poem: *"With a just scale that does not fall short by a barley grain, it has a witness from itself that is not unjust ('A'il)."* Likewise, 'Uthman bin 'Affan wrote to the people of Kufa: *"I am not a scale that does not tilt ('A'ul)."*

'A'ishah reported (in a narration elevated to the Prophet, and also related as a Mawquf statement from 'A'ishah herself) that she said regarding **{That (will make it) more likely that you will not be biased}**: *"Do not do injustice."* Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari recorded that Ibn 'Abbas, 'A'ishah, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Abu Razin, An-Nakha'i, Ash-Sha'bi, Ad-Dahhak, 'Ata' Al-Khurasani, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan all explained it as: *"Do not deviate."* Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari preferred and affirmed this majority view.

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's words: *{If you fear that you will not act fairly toward the orphan girls, marry what seems good to you of the women: two, or three, or four. But if you fear that you will not be fair, (marry only) one, or what your right (hands) own}* (4:3), Imam al-Tabari states that the most appropriate interpretation is: "If you fear that you will not act fairly toward the orphans, likewise you should fear concerning women, so do not marry from among them except those toward whom you do not fear that you will act unjustly, from one to four. **And if you fear injustice with one as well, then do not marry her; rather, you should resort to what your right hands own, for it is more likely that you will not act unjustly toward them.**"

Imam al-Tabari elaborates that Allah began the preceding verse prohibiting the unlawful consumption of orphans' property. Allah informed the believers that if they treat the matter of orphans as a sin, then what is obligatory upon them regarding the fear of Allah and treating the matter of women as a sin is identical. Allah made known how to avoid injustice toward women: Marry what is made lawful—two, three, or four. **"But if you also fear bringing injustice upon yourselves regarding the matter of one, in that you will not be able to treat her equitably, then do not marry her, but take concubines from the slaves. For it is more likely that you will not act unjustly toward them, because they are your property and your wealth, and you are not obligated to them with the rights like those you are obligated to free women. Thus, that would be closer for you to safety from sin and injustice."**

The classical authorities of interpretation concurred on this meaning of *{or what your right (hands) own}*:
- Qatadah explained: **"So if you fear that you will not be fair with one, then what your right hand owns."**
- Al-Suddi defined *{or what your right (hands) own}* as: **"Concubines."**
- Al-Rabi' likewise stated: **"So if you fear that you will not be fair with one, then what your right hand owns."**

Regarding Allah's statement *{That (will make it) more likely that you will not be biased}*, Imam al-Tabari concludes: If you fear that you will not be fair with two, three, or four, and so you marry one, or you fear that you will not be fair with one, and **"so you take as concubines the ownership of your right hands, then that is 'adna' (more likely), meaning: closer, 'that you will not be biased', He says: that you do not act unjustly and you do not deviate."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own. (This is) a written decree of God for you. (All women) beyond that are permitted to you to seek (to obtain) by means of your wealth, taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality. So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation. (There is) no blame on you in anything you may give them by mutual agreement beyond this obligation. Surely God is knowing, wise.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Revealed after the Battle of Hunayn/Awtas, this verse creates an exception allowing sexual relations with married women if captured in war. Enslavement automatically dissolves a captive woman's prior marriage without requiring a divorce once a waiting period (istibra') confirms non-pregnancy.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Prohibition of Married Women Except Captive Female Slaves

Allah says: **{And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own. (This is) a written decree of God for you. (All women) beyond that are permitted to you to seek (to obtain) by means of your wealth, taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality. So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation. (There is) no blame on you in anything you may give them by mutual agreement beyond this obligation. Surely God is knowing, wise.}**

Regarding Allah's statement: **{And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own}**, **the Ayah means: you are prohibited from marrying women who are already married, except those whom you acquire through captivity, for you are allowed to have sexual relations with them after making sure they are not pregnant, as the Ayah was revealed in that regard.**

Imam Ahmad, Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, and An-Nasa'i recorded from Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri: "**We captured some women from the area of Awtas who were already married, and we disliked having sexual relations with them because they already had husbands. So, we asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) about this matter, and this Ayah was revealed: {And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own.} Consequently, we considered their private parts lawful.**"

In another narration from Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri: "**The companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) captured female slaves on the day of Awtas who had husbands among the people of Shirk. It was as if some people from the companions of the Messenger of Allah held back and felt it would be a sin to have intercourse with them.** So this Ayah was revealed concerning that: **{And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own.}**" At-Tabarani also recorded from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning the captives of Khaybar with a similar meaning.

#### The Scholarly Dispute on the Sale of a Married Slave

**A group of the Salaf held the view that the sale of a female slave constitutes her divorce from her husband, taking from the general meaning of this Ayah.**
- Ibrahim An-Nakha'i reported that 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to say: "**Her sale is her divorce,**" reciting this Ayah: **{And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own.}** Ibn Mas'ud also stated: "**If a female slave is sold while she has a husband, her master has more right to her private parts.**"
- Qatadah reported that Ubayy bin Ka'b, Jabir bin 'Abdullah, and Ibn 'Abbas similarly declared: "**Her sale is her divorce.**"
- Ibn 'Abbas stated: "**The divorce of a female slave is six: her sale is her divorce, her emancipation is her divorce, gifting her is her divorce, absolving her is her divorce, and the divorce of her husband is her divorce.**"
- Sa'id bin al-Musayyib explained regarding the Ayah: "**They are women with husbands; Allah prohibited their marriage except what your right hands possess, so her sale is her divorce.**" Al-Hasan al-Basri likewise maintained: "**If she has a husband, her sale is her divorce,**" and: "**The sale of a female slave is her divorce and his sale is her divorce.**"

**The majority of scholars, both past and present, differed with them, and held the view that the sale of a female slave is not her divorce; because the buyer acts as a deputy for the seller, and the seller had already removed this benefit from his possession and sold her deprived of it. They relied on the Hadith of Barirah in the Sahih collections: 'A'ishah bought her and completed her emancipation, yet her marriage to her husband Mughith was not annulled. Rather, the Prophet (peace be upon him) gave her the choice between annulment and remaining with her husband, and she chose annulment. If the sale of a female slave were her divorce, the Prophet would not have given her the choice. Since he gave her the choice, it indicates the continuation of the marriage, and that the meaning of the Ayah refers specifically to captive women.**

Regarding Allah's statement: **{to seek (to obtain) by means of your wealth, taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality}**, **it means you are allowed to use your money to obtain up to four wives or as many female slaves as you wish, through legal means; this is why He said: {taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality.}**

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's statement: *{And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own}* (4:24), Imam al-Tabari explains that the meaning is: **forbidden to you are married women, except what your right hands own.**

### The Contextual Revelation Concerning the Captives of Awtas
The primary classical authorities transmitted that this verse was revealed regarding the female captives taken during the Battle of Awtas:
- Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated: **"That the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on the day of Hunayn sent an army to Awtas, and they met an enemy, and they took captive women who had husbands from among the polytheists. The Muslims felt it was a sin to have sexual relations with them, so Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed this verse: {And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own}, meaning, they are lawful to you when their waiting periods have concluded."**
- Abu Sa'id al-Khudri also recounted: **"When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, took captives from the people of Awtas, we said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how can we have relations with women whose lineages and husbands we already know?' Then this verse was revealed: {And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own}. So we considered their private parts lawful."**
- Qatadah reported from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: **"It was revealed on the day of Awtas, the Muslims took captives who had husbands in polytheism, so He said: {And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own}, He says: Except what Allah has given to you as spoils. Consequently we considered their private parts lawful by it."**

### The Legal View That Sale Nullifies Marriage
A group of early scholars held that sale dissolves the existing marriage of a female slave:
- 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud stated regarding *{And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own}*: **"Every woman with a husband is forbidden to you except if you buy her, or what your right hand possesses."** He also stated: **"Her sale is her divorce,"** reciting this verse, and affirmed: **"If a female slave is sold and she has a husband, then her master is more entitled to her private parts."**
- Ibn Abbas declared: **"The divorce of a female slave is six (ways): Her sale is her divorce, her manumission is her divorce, gifting her is her divorce, clearing her (of ties) is her divorce, and the divorce by her husband is her divorce."**

### Imam al-Tabari's Legal Synthesis and Ruling
Imam al-Tabari analyzes the linguistic root of *al-muhsanat* (chaste, protected, or married women), noting that protection (*ihsan*) occurs through marriage, freedom (*5:5*), Islam (*4:25*), or chastity (*24:4*). He delivers the comprehensive legal ruling:

**"Since He, the Blessed and Exalted, did not specify one muhsanah over another muhsanah in His saying: {And (also forbidden to you are) married women}, it is obligatory that every muhsanah, by whatever meanings of ihsan her ihsan might be, is forbidden to us in fornication or marriage, except what our right hands possess among them by purchase, as the Book of Allah, whose praise is exalted, has rendered lawful to us, or marriage according to what the revelation of Allah has left unrestricted for us."**

**"Thus, what He, the Blessed and Exalted, permitted for us in marriage from free women is four, other than those who are forbidden to us by lineage and affinity; and from female slaves, those whom we captured from the enemy, other than those whose circumstances align with the circumstances of the free women who are forbidden to us by lineage and affinity, for indeed they and the free women share the same circumstances regarding what is lawful and forbidden in that sense; and other than those whom we captured from the People of the Two Books who have husbands, for indeed captivity makes them lawful for the one who captured them after the waiting period (istibra'), and after extracting the right of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, which He established for the people of the Khumus out of them."**

Regarding a married slave who is sold, Imam al-Tabari clarifies that sale does not automatically dissolve marriage, citing the prophetic precedent of Barirah: **"As for the slave woman who has a husband, she is not lawful to her master except after her husband divorces her, or his death and the completion of her waiting period from him. As for her master selling her, it does not mandate separation between her and her husband, nor does it make her lawful for her buyer. This is due to the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: 'That he gave Barirah a choice when 'A'ishah emancipated her, between remaining with her husband to whom her masters had married her while she was in a state of slavery, and separating from him.'"**

Addressing the comprehensive meaning of right-hand possession (*milk al-yamin*), Imam al-Tabari writes:
**"If someone says: 'How can what is beyond the four, from the fifth to what is above them through marriage, be intended by the exception from His statement: {And (also forbidden to you are) married women}, while those married thereby are not owned?' It is said to him: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not restrict in His saying: {except what your right (hands) own} only those whose necks (bodies) are owned, excluding the one whose affair is owned over her through the marriage contract. Rather, He encompassed both meanings by His saying: {except what your right (hands) own}: I mean the ownership of the neck (slavery) and the ownership of enjoyment through marriage, because our right hands own all of that. As for the latter, it is ownership of enjoyment, and as for the former, it is ownership of service, enjoyment, and disposal in whatever is permitted to her master from her."**

Regarding the captives of Awtas, Imam al-Tabari notes:
**"If a reasoner among you presents as evidence the Hadith of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri that this verse was revealed regarding the captives of Awtas, it is said to him: Indeed, the captives of Awtas were not made lawful for relations through ownership and captivity exclusive of Islam. That is because they were polytheists from the idol worshippers, and the proof is established that the women of idol worshippers are not lawful through ownership exclusive of Islam, and that when they embraced Islam, Islam separated them from their husbands, whether they were captives or immigrants, except that if they were captives, they became lawful when they embraced Islam by the waiting period (istibra')."**

Imam al-Tabari concludes: **"If someone says: 'We know the permitted women who are besides those prohibited due to lineage and affinity. So who are the permitted among the married/chaste women (al-muhsanat), and who are the forbidden among them?' It is said: It is what is less than five, from one to four, based on what we mentioned from 'Ubaydah and Al-Suddi regarding free women. As for those other than women with husbands, they are not a restricted number through right hand ownership."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: Whoever among you cannot wait to marry believing, free women, (let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own. God knows your belief, (for) you are all alike. Marry them with the permission of their families, and give them their rightful marriage gifts, (as) married women, not (as) women who commit immorality or take secret lovers. But if they commit immorality after they are married, they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women. That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin. Yet to be patient (would be) better for you. God is forgiving, compassionate.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Permits impoverished free men to marry female slaves with master consent, though children inherit slave status. Halves the penal sanction (hadd) for slave adultery to 50 lashes and exempts slaves from death by stoning.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Marriage to Believing Slave Women and the Prescribed Penalties for Bondwomen

Allah says: **{Whoever among you cannot wait to marry believing, free women, (let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own. God knows your belief, (for) you are all alike. Marry them with the permission of their families, and give them their rightful marriage gifts, (as) married women, not (as) women who commit immorality or take secret lovers. But if they commit immorality after they are married, they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women. That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin. Yet to be patient (would be) better for you. God is forgiving, compassionate.}**

#### Requirements for Contracting Marriage with a Slave Woman

Allah states that those who do not possess **{the means}**—**meaning financial capability**—**{to marry believing, free women}**, may marry believing slave women. Rabi'ah suggested that "waiting" means desire, so one may marry a slave girl if his desire is for her. However, Allah rejects this notion by clarifying: **{(let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own}**, **meaning: they are allowed to wed believing slave girls owned by other believers.** Ibn 'Abbas, As-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan explained: "Let him marry from the slave girls of the believers."

Regarding Allah's statement: **{God knows your belief, (for) you are all alike}**, it means He knows the true reality and inner secrets of all things, whereas people judge only by outward appearance.

Regarding Allah's command: **{Marry them with the permission of their families}**, **it indicates that the owner is the guardian responsible for the slave girl, and consequently she cannot marry without his permission. The owner is likewise responsible for his male slave, who cannot wed without permission.** A Hadith affirms: "**Any male slave who marries without permission from his master is a fornicator.**" When the owner of a female slave is a woman, those who are authorized to act as guardians for the free woman are responsible for giving her slave girl in marriage.

Regarding His statement: **{and give them their rightful marriage gifts}**, it means: pay them their dowries willingly and with good grace, and do not withhold any portion of it by belittling them due to their status as owned slaves.

Regarding His statement: **{(as) married women, not (as) women who commit immorality or take secret lovers}**, it refers to chaste women who abstain from illicit sexual relations. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Mujahid, Ash-Sha'bi, Ad-Dahhak, 'Ata' Al-Khurasani, Yahya bin Abi Kathir, Muqatil, and As-Suddi explained that taking secret lovers refers to taking boyfriends, and Allah strictly forbade marrying women in such arrangements.

#### The Prescribed Punishment for a Slave Woman's Adultery

Regarding Allah's statement: **{But if they commit immorality after they are married, they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women}**:

The reciters differed concerning the verb *Uhsina*: some read it in the passive form (*Uhsina*—made chaste through marriage), while others read it in the active form (*Ahsana*—embracing Islam). Commentators held two primary views regarding its meaning:
1. *Ihsan* means embracing Islam. This was narrated from 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Anas, Al-Aswad bin Yazid, Zirr bin Hubaysh, Sa'id bin Jubayr, 'Ata', Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, Ash-Sha'bi, and As-Suddi, and is the view favored by Ash-Shafi'i.
2. *Ihsan* means marriage. This is the opinion of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Tawus, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Mujahid stated: "The *Ihsan* of the female slave is for a free man to marry her, and the *Ihsan* of the male slave is for a free woman to marry him." Ibn Kathir observes that this is the most apparent interpretation, because the entire Ayah is framed in the context of marrying believing slave women.

**The Position of the Majority**: **The majority of scholars hold that if a female slave commits fornication, she receives fifty lashes, whether she is a Muslim or a non-Muslim, married or unmarried.** The explicit prophetic traditions take precedence over any restrictive conditional implication:
- 'Ali ibn Abi Talib proclaimed in a sermon: "**O people, implement the prescribed punishment on your slaves, those of them who are married and those who are not married.** A female slave belonging to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) committed fornication, so he ordered me to flog her. Because she had recently given birth, I delayed until she recovered, and the Prophet approved, and she was flogged fifty times."
- Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "**If the female slave of one of you commits fornication and her fornication becomes evident, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and not berate her. Then if she commits fornication a second time, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and not berate her. Then if she commits fornication a third time... let him sell her, even if for a hair rope.**"
- 'Abdullah bin 'Ayyash reported: "'Umar bin Al-Khattab ordered me along with youths from Quraysh, so we flogged the slave girls of the emirate fifty lashes each for fornication."

**Other Juristic Positions**:
- Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, Sa'id bin Jubayr, and Abu 'Ubayd held that an unmarried slave girl receives disciplinary chastisement (Ta'zir), and only receives the prescribed fifty-lash Hadd when married.
- Dawud al-Zahiri held that an unmarried slave receives 100 lashes and a married slave receives 50 lashes—a view Ibn Kathir refutes as contrary to Shari'ah principles.
- Abu Thawr argued that a married slave girl must be stoned to death, whereas an unmarried slave receives fifty lashes. Ash-Shafi'i decisively refuted this, stating: "The Muslims did not differ that there is no stoning upon an owned slave for fornication." Allah's statement **{half the punishment (inflicted) on free women}** **indicates that the type of punishment prescribed here is the one that can be reduced to half—lashes in this case, not stoning to death.** Furthermore, when the slave woman Safiyyah committed fornication, 'Ali judged with the Prophet's ruling: *"The child belongs to the bed, and the fornicator gets the stone,"* and flogged both offenders fifty lashes each.

**Summary of Penalties for Female Slaves**:
- **Lashes**: **The established ruling is fifty lashes (half of the free unmarried woman's 100 lashes).**
- **Exile**: The majority of scholars ('Ali, the jurists of Madinah, Abu Hanifah, and Malik) hold that female slaves are not exiled, because exile contradicts the necessity of safeguarding and protecting them.

#### Conditions Restricting Marriage to Slave Girls

Regarding Allah's statement: **{That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin}**:
**This indicates that marrying slave girls, providing one satisfies the required conditions, is permissible only for those who fear falling into fornication**, and find it hard to remain patient. However, striving to remain chaste without marrying slave women is superior: **{Yet to be patient (would be) better for you. God is forgiving, compassionate.}** **For otherwise, if a man marries a slave woman, his offspring will become slaves to the woman's master—unless the husband is an Arab, in which case his children from her are free according to an old opinion of Ash-Shafi'i.**

**From this noble Ayah, the majority of scholars deduced that the permissibility of marrying slave girls requires two conditions: the absence of financial means to marry free women, and the fear of falling into sin (fornication). This is because marrying slave women causes the children to be born into bondage, and entails turning away from free women to slaves.** Abu Hanifah differed with the majority, holding that whenever a man is not married to a free woman, it is permissible for him to marry a Muslim or Kitabi slave girl regardless of wealth or fear of sin, relying on the general wording of Surah 5:5.

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's statement: *{And whoever among you cannot find the means to marry believing, free women, (let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own}* (4:25), Imam al-Tabari explains: **"He means by this: Whoever among you, O people, does not have the capability (tawlan)—meaning from among free men—to marry believing, free women (al-muhsanat), and they are free women who have believed in the Oneness of God and in the truth that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, brought."**

Early authorities clarified the terminology of the verse:
- Ibn Abbas stated regarding *{to marry believing, free women (al-muhsanat)}*: **"To marry free women, so let him marry from the slave girls of the believers."**
- Mujahid explained: **"'Al-muhsanat' are free women, so let him marry the believing slave girl."**
- Regarding the term "young women" (*al-fatayat*), it is linguistically noted: **"Then it is said to every female slave, whether older or youthful: 'young woman (fatah)', and to the male slave: 'young man (fata)'."**

### Marrying Slave Girls of the People of the Book
Imam al-Tabari rules regarding marrying non-Muslim slave girls: **"And the closer of the two views in that to what is correct is the statement of those who said: It is an indication of the prohibition of marrying the slave girls of the People of the Book, for they are not lawful except through right-hand possession. That is because God, exalted is His praise, made lawful the marriage of slave girls with conditions, so as long as the conditions He named regarding them are not met, it is not permissible for a Muslim to marry them."**

### Marriage with the Master's Permission and Dowries
Regarding the command *{Marry them with the permission of their families, and give them their rightful marriage gifts}*, Imam al-Tabari states: **"He means by His saying: 'Marry them (fa-nkihuhunna)', then wed them, and by His saying: 'with the permission of their families', with the permission of their masters, their instruction to you to marry them, and their consent; and He means by His saying: 'and give them their rightful marriage gifts', and give them their dowries based on what you have mutually agreed upon, from what God has made lawful for you, and permitted you to make as dowries for them."**

### Punitive Hadd Penalties and Halving the Punishment for Slaves
Regarding disciplinary and legal punishments upon slaves, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded: **"Establish the punishments upon what your right hands own."**

Imam al-Tabari explains: **"So he did not specify in that the one possessing a husband among them, nor the one without a husband. Thus the punishments are obligatory upon the masters of the slave girls to establish upon them, if they commit debauchery, by the Book of God and the command of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him."**

Abu Hurayrah and Zayd bin Khalid reported that the Prophet was asked concerning an unmarried slave girl who commits adultery: **"He said: 'Flog her. If she commits adultery, flog her. If she commits adultery, flog her. If she commits adultery—he said in the third or fourth—sell her, even if for a braided rope (dafir)'—and dafir is hair."**

Regarding Allah's ruling *{But if they commit immorality... they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women}*, Imam al-Tabari states:
**"He, exalted is His praise, means by His saying: 'But if they commit immorality (fa-in atayna bi-fahishatin)', so if your young women come—and they are your slave girls—after they are protected by Islam, or they are protected by marriage to immorality, and it is adultery: 'they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women', he says: they will be liable to half of what is on free women of the prescribed punishment, if they commit adultery before Ihsan (protection) by husbands."**

**"And the 'punishment' which God, blessed and exalted, mentioned in this place is the prescribed punishment (Hadd). And that half which God appointed as punishment for whoever commits immorality among the slave women if they are protected (uhsinna) is: fifty lashes, and banishment for six months, and that is half a year. Because the mandatory punishment on a free woman if she commits immorality before Ihsan by a husband is flogging with one hundred lashes and banishment for one year. Thus the half of that is fifty lashes, and banishment for half a year. And that is what God made as punishment for protected slave women if they commit immorality."**

Qatadah affirmed regarding this penalty: **"Fifty lashes, and neither banishment nor stoning."**

### Marrying Slave Girls Permitted Only for Those Fearing Sin, Patience Preferred
Regarding *{That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin}*, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"He, exalted is His mention, means by His saying: 'That', this which I have made lawful, O people, from the marriage of your believing young women for whoever among you does not have the capability to marry believing, free women—I have made it lawful for those of you who fear sin, excluding others who do not fear sin."** Mujahid noted that "sin" here refers to: **"Adultery."**

Regarding *{Yet to be patient (would be) better for you}*, Imam al-Tabari concludes: **"He, exalted is His praise, means by that: 'Yet to be patient', O people, from marrying slave girls, 'would be better for you'. 'God is forgiving' toward you concerning the marriage of slave girls that you marry them based on what He has made lawful for you and permitted you, and what has passed from you in that, if you rectify the affairs of yourselves between you and God; 'compassionate' toward you, as He permitted you to marry them upon impoverishment and lack of capability for a free woman."**

Al-Suddi explained why patience is superior: **"That you be patient and not marry a slave girl resulting in your children being owned slaves, it is better for you."**

verses.key_legal_rulings: Establishes that lawful sexual relations are strictly confined to two categories: married free wives and owned female slave concubines. Sexual cohabitation with right-hand possessions carries zero religious blame or legal liability for male masters.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Guarding the Private Parts Except with Wives and Concubines

Allah says: **{And those who guard their private parts. Except from their wives or what their right (hands) own, for then, they are free from blame. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.}** [23:5-7]

**This means: those who protect their private parts from unlawful actions and do not do that which Allah has forbidden—fornication and homosexuality—and do not approach anyone except the wives whom Allah has made permissible for them, or their right hand possessions from the captives. One who seeks what Allah has made permissible for him is not to be blamed and there is no sin on him.** For this reason Allah says: **{for then, they are free from blame. But whoever seeks beyond that}**, **meaning: other than a wife or slave girl**, **{then those are the transgressors}**, **meaning: aggressors.**

Qatadah reported that a woman took her male slave as a sexual partner and claimed: "I interpreted an Ayah from the Book of Allah: {or what their right hands possess}." When she was brought to 'Umar bin Al-Khattab, the Companions of the Prophet said: **"She interpreted an Ayah from the Book of Allah in a way other than its true meaning." So 'Umar banished the slave, shaved his head, and declared to the woman: "After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim."** Ibn Kathir notes: **'Umar only made her unlawful for men in order to treat her with the opposite of her illicit intent.**

**Imam Ash-Shafi'i and those who agreed with him used this noble Ayah as evidence for the prohibition of masturbation (with the hand): {And those who guard their private parts. Except from their wives or what their right hands possess. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.}** He explained that this act falls outside of these two lawful categories. They also cited the Hadith transmitted by Al-Hasan bin 'Arafah from Anas bin Malik that the Prophet (peace be upon him) condemned those who mate with their hands alongside other major sins, though its chain contains obscure narrators.

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's words describing the believers: *{and who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed}* (23:5-6), Imam al-Tabari provides a comprehensive breakdown:

Regarding *{and who guard their private parts}*, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"And those who, for their own private parts—and He meant by the private parts in this place: the private parts of men, and that is their front parts—guard, they guard them from employing them in any of the private parts."**

Regarding *{except from their wives}*, he states: **"Except from their wives whom Allah has made permissible for men through marriage."**

Regarding *{or what their right (hands) own}*, he defines: **"He means by that: their female slaves. And 'what' in His saying: (or what their right (hands) own) is in the position of the genitive case, in conjunction with 'wives'."**

Regarding *{surely then they are not (to be) blamed}*, Imam al-Tabari rules: **"Thus, whoever does not guard his private part from his wife and his right hand possession, and guards it from the rest of creation, he is neither rebuked for that, nor condemned, nor is he, by doing that, committing a sin for which he is to be blamed."**

The early commentators confirmed this consensus. Ibn Abbas stated regarding this verse: **"Allah has approved for them to approach their wives and what their right hands own."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have granted their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and paternal aunts, your maternal uncles and maternal aunts, who have emigrated with you, and any believing woman, if she gives herself to the prophet, and if the prophet wishes to take her in marriage. (That is) exclusively for you, apart from the believers – We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives and what their right (hands) own – so that there may be no blame on you. God is forgiving, compassionate.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Authorizes the Prophet to take female captives granted as war spoils (fay') as concubines. While restricting ordinary believers to four free wives, Islamic jurisprudence derives from this verse their unrestricted right to limitless slave concubinage.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### The Women Made Lawful for the Prophet and the Believers' Concubinage Limits

Allah addresses His Prophet stating that He has made lawful for him his wives to whom he has given their marriage gifts (*Mahr*), referred to here as '*Ujur*' (rewards), as stated by Mujahid and other scholars. The *Mahr* the Prophet gave to his wives was twelve *Uqiyah* and a *Nash* (five hundred Dirhams), except for Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, for whom An-Najashi paid four hundred Dinars on his behalf. **Also excepted is Safiyyah bint Huyayy, whom he chose from the captives of Khaybar, then freed her and made her emancipation her *Mahr*. The same was the case with Juwayriyah bint Al-Harith Al-Mustaliqiyyah, for whom he paid off her contract of manumission to Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas and married her.**

Regarding Allah's statement: **{and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you}**, **it means: He also permitted you to take concubines from what you have taken from the war booty. He owned Safiyyah and Juwayriyah, then freed them and married them. He also owned Rayhanah bint Sham'un An-Nadariyyah, and Mariyah Al-Qibtiyyah, the mother of his son Ibrahim; and they were among his concubines.**

Scholars including Muhammad bin Ka'b, 'Umar bin Al-Hakam, and 'Abdullah bin 'Ubaydah enumerated the Prophet's marriages, including **the two captives: Safiyyah bint Huyayy bin Akhtab, and Juwayriyah bint Al-Harith bin 'Amr bin Al-Mustaliq Al-Khuza'iyyah.**

Regarding Allah's statement: **{We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives and what their right (hands) own}**, Ubayy bin Ka'b, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir explained **it means: "Regarding limiting them to four free women and whatever concubines they wish, and stipulating the conditions of a guardian, a *Mahr*, and witnesses for them—meaning the *Ummah* (the Muslim nation). But We have granted you an exception in that, so We did not make any of that obligatory upon you, so that there may be no blame on you. God is forgiving, compassionate."**

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's address to the Prophet: *{O Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have granted their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you as spoils of war...}* (33:50), Imam al-Tabari elucidates the operative rulings:

Regarding *{their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you}*, Imam al-Tabari states: **"And We have made lawful for you your female slaves whom you have taken as captives, and thus owned them through captivity, and who have become yours due to the conquests God bestowed upon you as spoils of war."**

Regarding the distinction between the Prophet and the believers in *{exclusively for you, apart from the believers}*, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"It is mentioned that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, before this verse was revealed to him, could marry whichever women he wished. Then God restricted him to these, so he did not exceed them, and He restricted the rest of his nation to two, three, and four."**

Regarding *{We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives}*, Imam al-Tabari states: **"We know what We have made obligatory upon the believers concerning their wives if they wish to marry them, from that which We have not made obligatory upon you, and the rulings We have specified for them regarding that to your exclusion. This is that We have made it obligatory for them that a marriage contract with a free Muslim woman is not lawful except with a paternal guardian (wali 'asabah) and just witnesses, and it is not lawful for them to have more than four of them."**

Qatadah affirmed this distinction: **"It was part of what God made obligatory upon them that a woman is not married except with a guardian and a dowry in the presence of two just witnesses, and not more than four women are lawful to them, [in addition to] what their right hands possess."**

Regarding *{and what their right (hands) own}*, Imam al-Tabari delivers the legal ruling for believers: **"We know what We have made obligatory for the believers concerning their wives, because it is not lawful for them to have more than four of them, and what their right hands possess. For all of them, if they are believing women or women of the Book, are lawful to them through captivity, concubinage, and other methods of ownership."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you, nor (is it permitted to you) to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you, except for what your right (hand) owns. God is watching over everything.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Prohibits the Prophet from marrying additional free wives or exchanging existing ones, while explicitly exempting female slave concubines. Confirms that marital caps and restrictions governing free wives never applied to the acquisition of slave chattel.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Restrictions on Additional Marriages and the Unrestricted Exemption for Concubines

Scholars including Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari stated that this Ayah was revealed as an honor and reward to the wives of the Prophet for choosing Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter when given the choice. **When they chose the Messenger of Allah, their reward was that Allah restricted him to them, and forbade him to marry anyone else or to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleased him, with the exception of female slaves and concubines, regarding whom there was no restriction.** **Then Allah lifted the restriction on him in that regard and abrogated the prohibition, permitting him to marry, but he did not marry any other women after that, so that the favor of the Messenger of Allah upon them would remain.**

Other commentators explained that Allah's statement: **{Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you}** **means: beyond the lawful categories previously specified—wives who were paid their dowries, those whom your right hand possesses from captives**, cousin emigrants, and the woman who offers herself; all categories outside of these were made unlawful to him.

Ibn 'Abbas explained: "The Messenger of Allah was forbidden from certain categories of women, except the believing emigrant women, by His saying: **{Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you, nor to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you, except for what your right (hand) owns.}** **So Allah made lawful for him believing slave girls and {a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet}**, while making unlawful women outside these categories."

Regarding His statement: **{nor to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you}**, **it means He forbade him from adding to them, or divorcing one of them and exchanging her for another, except for what his right hand possesses of female slaves, for which there was no restriction.**

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's statement: *{Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you, nor (is it permitted to you) to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you, except for what your right (hand) owns. God is watching over everything}* (33:52), Imam al-Tabari presents the authoritative interpretation:

**"The meaning of that is: Women are not permitted to you after—after those whom I have permitted to you by My saying {Indeed We have permitted to you your wives to whom you have given their compensations...} until His saying {and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet}."**

He further explains that the verse specifically details: **"his wives, what his right hand owns that God returns to him, the daughters of his paternal uncle and his paternal aunts, the daughters of his maternal uncle and his maternal aunts who emigrated with him, and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet, making the disbelieving women specifically forbidden—then what we have said regarding that is established as correct, to the exclusion of the statement of the one who opposed our statement regarding it."**

Analyzing the syntactic structure and the explicit exception granted for female slaves, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"And {except} in His saying {except for what your right (hand) owns} is an exception from 'women'. And the meaning of that is: Women are not permitted to you after those whom I have permitted to you except what your right hand owns of slave girls, for you have the right to own slave girls from whichever of the races of people you wish."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: {'hafs_verse_id': '70:29-30', 'verses': [{'hafs_verse_id': '70:29', 'text': 'and who guard their private parts,'}, {'hafs_verse_id': '70:30', 'text': 'except concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed,'}], 'combined_text': 'and who guard their private parts, except concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed,'}
verses.key_legal_rulings: Codifies chastity as a core religious duty while maintaining an explicit exemption for wives and owned female slaves. Formally classifies sexual access to slave concubines as lawful alongside legal marriage, free of moral or religious blame.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Guarding the Private Parts Except with Wives and Female Slaves

Regarding Allah's statement: **{And who guard their private parts}** [70:29], **it means: they keep their private parts away from that which is forbidden, and prevent them from being placed in anything other than what Allah has allowed.**

This is why Allah says: **{Except concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own—surely then they are not (to be) blamed}** [70:30], **meaning: except with their wives or their female slave concubines, for in those relations they are not blameworthy.**

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's statement describing the righteous: *{and who guard their private parts, except concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed}* (70:29-30), Imam al-Tabari explains:

Regarding *{and who guard their private parts}*, he states: **"meaning: they guard their front parts from everything that Allah has forbidden them to place them in."**

Regarding the lawful exception, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"Except that they are not blameworthy in leaving their guarding, concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own of their female slaves."**

Analyzing the linguistic nuance of the text, he clarifies that although no explicit negative particle precedes the exception, the subsequent clause **"surely then they are not (to be) blamed"** indicates an implied negation in the construction. This is analogous in Arabic to saying: 'Do what seems fit to you except committing disobedience, for you will be punished for it,' with the understood meaning being: 'Do what seems fit to you, except that you will be punished for committing disobedience.'

verses.theme: Slavery as Chattel Property & Master's Maintenance Duties
verses.droge_translation: Serve God, and do not associate anything with Him, and (do) good to parents and to family, and the orphans and the poor, and the neighbor who is related and the neighbor who is a stranger, and the companion at your side, and the traveler, and what your right (hands) own. Surely God does not love anyone who is arrogant (and) boastful,
verses.key_legal_rulings: Legislates benevolence and maintenance toward owned slaves as household dependents under master jurisdiction. Establishes legal duties for owners to provide food, shelter, and appropriate workloads, reflecting the master's comprehensive property rights over chattel.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Regarding Allah's command: *{and what your right (hands) own}* (4:36), **this is an order to be kind to slaves, because the slave is weak and helpless, held as a captive in the hands of people.**

Because of this, an authentic Hadith records that during the illness that preceded his death, the Messenger of Allah continued advising his Ummah: **"(Protect) the prayer, (protect) the prayer, and (those slaves) what your right hands possess."** He repeated it continuously until his tongue could no longer speak it.

Al-Miqdam bin Ma'dikarib narrated that the Messenger of Allah said: **"What you feed yourself is a Sadaqah (charity) for you, what you feed your children is Sadaqah for you, what you feed your wife is Sadaqah for you, and what you feed your servant is Sadaqah for you."** (Recorded by Ahmad and An-Nasa'i with an authentic chain).

'Abdullah bin 'Amr asked his caretaker, "Did you give the slaves their food yet?" When he answered no, Ibn 'Amr instructed: "Go and give it to them, for the Messenger of Allah said: **'It is enough sin for someone to prevent whomever he is responsible for from getting their food.'**" (Recorded by Muslim).

Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet said: **"The slave has the right to have food and clothing, and is only required to perform what he can bear of work."** (Recorded by Muslim). Abu Hurayrah also narrated that the Prophet said: **"When your servant brings meals to one of you, if he does not let him sit with him, then he should hand him a mouthful or two mouthfuls, or a meal or two, for he managed its heat and preparation."** (Recorded in the Two Sahihs; Muslim's wording adds: "let him seat him with him to eat, and if the food is a small amount, let him place in his hand a meal or two").

Abu Dharr narrated that the Prophet said: **"They are your brothers and your servants whom Allah has placed under your hands. Whoever has his brother under his hand, he should feed him from what he eats, and clothe him from what he wears, and do not burden them with what overcomes them; and if you burden them, then help them."** (Recorded in the Two Sahihs).

tafsir_tabari.text:
### Interpretation of "What Your Right Hands Own"

Regarding the interpretation of His statement: **{and what your right (hands) own}**, Abu Ja'far al-Tabari explains: By that, He, may His praise be exalted, means: **And those whom you possess from your slaves.** Thus He attributed possession to the "right hand," just as it is said: "your mouth spoke," "your foot walked," and "your hand grasped," meaning: you spoke, you walked, and you grasped.

However, as for what each limb is described with from that, it is only attributed to that limb because the action happens through it, according to what is mutually known among people, exclusive from the rest of the body's faculties. Thus it becomes known—by describing that limb with what it was described with—what meaning is intended from the speech.

The same applies to His statement: **{and what your right (hands) own}**, because **the slaves belonging to any of us are under his hands, and they only eat what our right hands hand over, and wear what they clothe them with, and you direct them in whatever you love to direct them in with it.** So their possession is attributed to the "right hands" for that reason.

Mujahid commented regarding *{and what your right (hands) own}*: "From what God has bestowed upon you. All of this, God has enjoined."

Abu Ja'far al-Tabari explains: Mujahid only means by his saying, "All of this, God has enjoined," the parents, the relatives of kinship, the orphans, the poor, the neighbor who is related, the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion at your side, and the traveler. **Thus our Lord, Exalted is His Majesty, enjoined His servants to do good towards all of these, and commanded His creation to preserve His directive regarding them.** Therefore, it is a duty upon His servants to preserve the directive of God regarding them, and then to preserve the directive of His Messenger, may God's peace and blessings be upon him.

### The Condemnation of the Arrogant and Boastful Master

Regarding the interpretation of His statement: **{Surely God does not love anyone who is arrogant (and) boastful}** (36), Abu Ja'far al-Tabari explains: He means by His statement, may His praise be exalted, that God does not love anyone who possesses conceit (*khuyala'*).
