Rather, He encompassed both meanings by His saying: {except what your right (hands) own}: I mean the ownership of the neck (slavery) and the ownership of enjoyment through marriage, because our right hands own all of that. As for the latter, it is ownership of enjoyment, and as for the former, it is ownership of service, enjoyment, and disposal in whatever is permitted to her master from her."**

Regarding the captives of Awtas, Imam al-Tabari notes:
**"If a reasoner among you presents as evidence the Hadith of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri that this verse was revealed regarding the captives of Awtas, it is said to him: Indeed, the captives of Awtas were not made lawful for relations through ownership and captivity exclusive of Islam. That is because they were polytheists from the idol worshippers, and the proof is established that the women of idol worshippers are not lawful through ownership exclusive of Islam, and that when they embraced Islam, Islam separated them from their husbands, whether they were captives or immigrants, except that if they were captives, they became lawful when they embraced Islam by the waiting period (istibra')."**

Imam al-Tabari concludes: **"If someone says: 'We know the permitted women who are besides those prohibited due to lineage and affinity. So who are the permitted among the married/chaste women (al-muhsanat), and who are the forbidden among them?' It is said: It is what is less than five, from one to four, based on what we mentioned from 'Ubaydah and Al-Suddi regarding free women. As for those other than women with husbands, they are not a restricted number through right hand ownership."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: Whoever among you cannot wait to marry believing, free women, (let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own. God knows your belief, (for) you are all alike. Marry them with the permission of their families, and give them their rightful marriage gifts, (as) married women, not (as) women who commit immorality or take secret lovers. But if they commit immorality after they are married, they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women. That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin. Yet to be patient (would be) better for you. God is forgiving, compassionate.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Permits impoverished free men to marry female slaves with master consent, though children inherit slave status. Halves the penal sanction (hadd) for slave adultery to 50 lashes and exempts slaves from death by stoning.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Marriage to Believing Slave Women and the Prescribed Penalties for Bondwomen

Allah says: **{Whoever among you cannot wait to marry believing, free women, (let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own. God knows your belief, (for) you are all alike. Marry them with the permission of their families, and give them their rightful marriage gifts, (as) married women, not (as) women who commit immorality or take secret lovers. But if they commit immorality after they are married, they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women. That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin. Yet to be patient (would be) better for you. God is forgiving, compassionate.}**

#### Requirements for Contracting Marriage with a Slave Woman

Allah states that those who do not possess **{the means}**—**meaning financial capability**—**{to marry believing, free women}**, may marry believing slave women. Rabi'ah suggested that "waiting" means desire, so one may marry a slave girl if his desire is for her. However, Allah rejects this notion by clarifying: **{(let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own}**, **meaning: they are allowed to wed believing slave girls owned by other believers.** Ibn 'Abbas, As-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan explained: "Let him marry from the slave girls of the believers."

Regarding Allah's statement: **{God knows your belief, (for) you are all alike}**, it means He knows the true reality and inner secrets of all things, whereas people judge only by outward appearance.

Regarding Allah's command: **{Marry them with the permission of their families}**, **it indicates that the owner is the guardian responsible for the slave girl, and consequently she cannot marry without his permission. The owner is likewise responsible for his male slave, who cannot wed without permission.** A Hadith affirms: "**Any male slave who marries without permission from his master is a fornicator.**" When the owner of a female slave is a woman, those who are authorized to act as guardians for the free woman are responsible for giving her slave girl in marriage.

Regarding His statement: **{and give them their rightful marriage gifts}**, it means: pay them their dowries willingly and with good grace, and do not withhold any portion of it by belittling them due to their status as owned slaves.

Regarding His statement: **{(as) married women, not (as) women who commit immorality or take secret lovers}**, it refers to chaste women who abstain from illicit sexual relations. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Mujahid, Ash-Sha'bi, Ad-Dahhak, 'Ata' Al-Khurasani, Yahya bin Abi Kathir, Muqatil, and As-Suddi explained that taking secret lovers refers to taking boyfriends, and Allah strictly forbade marrying women in such arrangements.

#### The Prescribed Punishment for a Slave Woman's Adultery

Regarding Allah's statement: **{But if they commit immorality after they are married, they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women}**:

The reciters differed concerning the verb *Uhsina*: some read it in the passive form (*Uhsina*—made chaste through marriage), while others read it in the active form (*Ahsana*—embracing Islam). Commentators held two primary views regarding its meaning:
1. *Ihsan* means embracing Islam. This was narrated from 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Anas, Al-Aswad bin Yazid, Zirr bin Hubaysh, Sa'id bin Jubayr, 'Ata', Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, Ash-Sha'bi, and As-Suddi, and is the view favored by Ash-Shafi'i.
2. *Ihsan* means marriage. This is the opinion of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Tawus, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Mujahid stated: "The *Ihsan* of the female slave is for a free man to marry her, and the *Ihsan* of the male slave is for a free woman to marry him." Ibn Kathir observes that this is the most apparent interpretation, because the entire Ayah is framed in the context of marrying believing slave women.

**The Position of the Majority**: **The majority of scholars hold that if a female slave commits fornication, she receives fifty lashes, whether she is a Muslim or a non-Muslim, married or unmarried.** The explicit prophetic traditions take precedence over any restrictive conditional implication:
- 'Ali ibn Abi Talib proclaimed in a sermon: "**O people, implement the prescribed punishment on your slaves, those of them who are married and those who are not married.** A female slave belonging to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) committed fornication, so he ordered me to flog her. Because she had recently given birth, I delayed until she recovered, and the Prophet approved, and she was flogged fifty times."
- Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "**If the female slave of one of you commits fornication and her fornication becomes evident, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and not berate her. Then if she commits fornication a second time, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and not berate her. Then if she commits fornication a third time... let him sell her, even if for a hair rope.**"
- 'Abdullah bin 'Ayyash reported: "'Umar bin Al-Khattab ordered me along with youths from Quraysh, so we flogged the slave girls of the emirate fifty lashes each for fornication."

**Other Juristic Positions**:
- Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, Sa'id bin Jubayr, and Abu 'Ubayd held that an unmarried slave girl receives disciplinary chastisement (Ta'zir), and only receives the prescribed fifty-lash Hadd when married.
- Dawud al-Zahiri held that an unmarried slave receives 100 lashes and a married slave receives 50 lashes—a view Ibn Kathir refutes as contrary to Shari'ah principles.
- Abu Thawr argued that a married slave girl must be stoned to death, whereas an unmarried slave receives fifty lashes. Ash-Shafi'i decisively refuted this, stating: "The Muslims did not differ that there is no stoning upon an owned slave for fornication." Allah's statement **{half the punishment (inflicted) on free women}** **indicates that the type of punishment prescribed here is the one that can be reduced to half—lashes in this case, not stoning to death.** Furthermore, when the slave woman Safiyyah committed fornication, 'Ali judged with the Prophet's ruling: *"The child belongs to the bed, and the fornicator gets the stone,"* and flogged both offenders fifty lashes each.

**Summary of Penalties for Female Slaves**:
- **Lashes**: **The established ruling is fifty lashes (half of the free unmarried woman's 100 lashes).**
- **Exile**: The majority of scholars ('Ali, the jurists of Madinah, Abu Hanifah, and Malik) hold that female slaves are not exiled, because exile contradicts the necessity of safeguarding and protecting them.

#### Conditions Restricting Marriage to Slave Girls

Regarding Allah's statement: **{That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin}**:
**This indicates that marrying slave girls, providing one satisfies the required conditions, is permissible only for those who fear falling into fornication**, and find it hard to remain patient. However, striving to remain chaste without marrying slave women is superior: **{Yet to be patient (would be) better for you. God is forgiving, compassionate.}** **For otherwise, if a man marries a slave woman, his offspring will become slaves to the woman's master—unless the husband is an Arab, in which case his children from her are free according to an old opinion of Ash-Shafi'i.**

**From this noble Ayah, the majority of scholars deduced that the permissibility of marrying slave girls requires two conditions: the absence of financial means to marry free women, and the fear of falling into sin (fornication). This is because marrying slave women causes the children to be born into bondage, and entails turning away from free women to slaves.** Abu Hanifah differed with the majority, holding that whenever a man is not married to a free woman, it is permissible for him to marry a Muslim or Kitabi slave girl regardless of wealth or fear of sin, relying on the general wording of Surah 5:5.

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's statement: *{And whoever among you cannot find the means to marry believing, free women, (let them take) believing young women from what your right (hands) own}* (4:25), Imam al-Tabari explains: **"He means by this: Whoever among you, O people, does not have the capability (tawlan)—meaning from among free men—to marry believing, free women (al-muhsanat), and they are free women who have believed in the Oneness of God and in the truth that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, brought."**

Early authorities clarified the terminology of the verse:
- Ibn Abbas stated regarding *{to marry believing, free women (al-muhsanat)}*: **"To marry free women, so let him marry from the slave girls of the believers."**
- Mujahid explained: **"'Al-muhsanat' are free women, so let him marry the believing slave girl."**
- Regarding the term "young women" (*al-fatayat*), it is linguistically noted: **"Then it is said to every female slave, whether older or youthful: 'young woman (fatah)', and to the male slave: 'young man (fata)'."**

### Marrying Slave Girls of the People of the Book
Imam al-Tabari rules regarding marrying non-Muslim slave girls: **"And the closer of the two views in that to what is correct is the statement of those who said: It is an indication of the prohibition of marrying the slave girls of the People of the Book, for they are not lawful except through right-hand possession. That is because God, exalted is His praise, made lawful the marriage of slave girls with conditions, so as long as the conditions He named regarding them are not met, it is not permissible for a Muslim to marry them."**

### Marriage with the Master's Permission and Dowries
Regarding the command *{Marry them with the permission of their families, and give them their rightful marriage gifts}*, Imam al-Tabari states: **"He means by His saying: 'Marry them (fa-nkihuhunna)', then wed them, and by His saying: 'with the permission of their families', with the permission of their masters, their instruction to you to marry them, and their consent; and He means by His saying: 'and give them their rightful marriage gifts', and give them their dowries based on what you have mutually agreed upon, from what God has made lawful for you, and permitted you to make as dowries for them."**

### Punitive Hadd Penalties and Halving the Punishment for Slaves
Regarding disciplinary and legal punishments upon slaves, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded: **"Establish the punishments upon what your right hands own."**

Imam al-Tabari explains: **"So he did not specify in that the one possessing a husband among them, nor the one without a husband. Thus the punishments are obligatory upon the masters of the slave girls to establish upon them, if they commit debauchery, by the Book of God and the command of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him."**

Abu Hurayrah and Zayd bin Khalid reported that the Prophet was asked concerning an unmarried slave girl who commits adultery: **"He said: 'Flog her. If she commits adultery, flog her. If she commits adultery, flog her. If she commits adultery—he said in the third or fourth—sell her, even if for a braided rope (dafir)'—and dafir is hair."**

Regarding Allah's ruling *{But if they commit immorality... they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women}*, Imam al-Tabari states:
**"He, exalted is His praise, means by His saying: 'But if they commit immorality (fa-in atayna bi-fahishatin)', so if your young women come—and they are your slave girls—after they are protected by Islam, or they are protected by marriage to immorality, and it is adultery: 'they will be liable to half the punishment (inflicted) on free women', he says: they will be liable to half of what is on free women of the prescribed punishment, if they commit adultery before Ihsan (protection) by husbands."**

**"And the 'punishment' which God, blessed and exalted, mentioned in this place is the prescribed punishment (Hadd). And that half which God appointed as punishment for whoever commits immorality among the slave women if they are protected (uhsinna) is: fifty lashes, and banishment for six months, and that is half a year. Because the mandatory punishment on a free woman if she commits immorality before Ihsan by a husband is flogging with one hundred lashes and banishment for one year. Thus the half of that is fifty lashes, and banishment for half a year. And that is what God made as punishment for protected slave women if they commit immorality."**

Qatadah affirmed regarding this penalty: **"Fifty lashes, and neither banishment nor stoning."**

### Marrying Slave Girls Permitted Only for Those Fearing Sin, Patience Preferred
Regarding *{That (provision) is for those of you who fear sin}*, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"He, exalted is His mention, means by His saying: 'That', this which I have made lawful, O people, from the marriage of your believing young women for whoever among you does not have the capability to marry believing, free women—I have made it lawful for those of you who fear sin, excluding others who do not fear sin."** Mujahid noted that "sin" here refers to: **"Adultery."**

Regarding *{Yet to be patient (would be) better for you}*, Imam al-Tabari concludes: **"He, exalted is His praise, means by that: 'Yet to be patient', O people, from marrying slave girls, 'would be better for you'. 'God is forgiving' toward you concerning the marriage of slave girls that you marry them based on what He has made lawful for you and permitted you, and what has passed from you in that, if you rectify the affairs of yourselves between you and God; 'compassionate' toward you, as He permitted you to marry them upon impoverishment and lack of capability for a free woman."**

Al-Suddi explained why patience is superior: **"That you be patient and not marry a slave girl resulting in your children being owned slaves, it is better for you."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: {'hafs_verse_id': '23:5-6', 'verses': [{'hafs_verse_id': '23:5', 'text': 'and who guard their private parts,'}, {'hafs_verse_id': '23:6', 'text': 'except from their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed,'}], 'combined_text': 'and who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed,'}
verses.key_legal_rulings: Establishes that lawful sexual relations are strictly confined to two categories: married free wives and owned female slave concubines. Sexual cohabitation with right-hand possessions carries zero religious blame or legal liability for male masters.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Guarding the Private Parts Except with Wives and Concubines

Allah says: **{And those who guard their private parts. Except from their wives or what their right (hands) own, for then, they are free from blame. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.}** [23:5-7]

**This means: those who protect their private parts from unlawful actions and do not do that which Allah has forbidden—fornication and homosexuality—and do not approach anyone except the wives whom Allah has made permissible for them, or their right hand possessions from the captives. One who seeks what Allah has made permissible for him is not to be blamed and there is no sin on him.** For this reason Allah says: **{for then, they are free from blame. But whoever seeks beyond that}**, **meaning: other than a wife or slave girl**, **{then those are the transgressors}**, **meaning: aggressors.**

Qatadah reported that a woman took her male slave as a sexual partner and claimed: "I interpreted an Ayah from the Book of Allah: {or what their right hands possess}." When she was brought to 'Umar bin Al-Khattab, the Companions of the Prophet said: **"She interpreted an Ayah from the Book of Allah in a way other than its true meaning." So 'Umar banished the slave, shaved his head, and declared to the woman: "After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim."** Ibn Kathir notes: **'Umar only made her unlawful for men in order to treat her with the opposite of her illicit intent.**

**Imam Ash-Shafi'i and those who agreed with him used this noble Ayah as evidence for the prohibition of masturbation (with the hand): {And those who guard their private parts. Except from their wives or what their right hands possess. But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.}** He explained that this act falls outside of these two lawful categories. They also cited the Hadith transmitted by Al-Hasan bin 'Arafah from Anas bin Malik that the Prophet (peace be upon him) condemned those who mate with their hands alongside other major sins, though its chain contains obscure narrators.

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's words describing the believers: *{and who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed}* (23:5-6), Imam al-Tabari provides a comprehensive breakdown:

Regarding *{and who guard their private parts}*, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"And those who, for their own private parts—and He meant by the private parts in this place: the private parts of men, and that is their front parts—guard, they guard them from employing them in any of the private parts."**

Regarding *{except from their wives}*, he states: **"Except from their wives whom Allah has made permissible for men through marriage."**

Regarding *{or what their right (hands) own}*, he defines: **"He means by that: their female slaves. And 'what' in His saying: (or what their right (hands) own) is in the position of the genitive case, in conjunction with 'wives'."**

Regarding *{surely then they are not (to be) blamed}*, Imam al-Tabari rules: **"Thus, whoever does not guard his private part from his wife and his right hand possession, and guards it from the rest of creation, he is neither rebuked for that, nor condemned, nor is he, by doing that, committing a sin for which he is to be blamed."**

The early commentators confirmed this consensus. Ibn Abbas stated regarding this verse: **"Allah has approved for them to approach their wives and what their right hands own."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have granted their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and paternal aunts, your maternal uncles and maternal aunts, who have emigrated with you, and any believing woman, if she gives herself to the prophet, and if the prophet wishes to take her in marriage. (That is) exclusively for you, apart from the believers – We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives and what their right (hands) own – so that there may be no blame on you. God is forgiving, compassionate.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Authorizes the Prophet to take female captives granted as war spoils (fay') as concubines. While restricting ordinary believers to four free wives, Islamic jurisprudence derives from this verse their unrestricted right to limitless slave concubinage.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### The Women Made Lawful for the Prophet and the Believers' Concubinage Limits

Allah addresses His Prophet stating that He has made lawful for him his wives to whom he has given their marriage gifts (*Mahr*), referred to here as '*Ujur*' (rewards), as stated by Mujahid and other scholars. The *Mahr* the Prophet gave to his wives was twelve *Uqiyah* and a *Nash* (five hundred Dirhams), except for Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, for whom An-Najashi paid four hundred Dinars on his behalf. **Also excepted is Safiyyah bint Huyayy, whom he chose from the captives of Khaybar, then freed her and made her emancipation her *Mahr*. The same was the case with Juwayriyah bint Al-Harith Al-Mustaliqiyyah, for whom he paid off her contract of manumission to Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas and married her.**

Regarding Allah's statement: **{and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you}**, **it means: He also permitted you to take concubines from what you have taken from the war booty. He owned Safiyyah and Juwayriyah, then freed them and married them. He also owned Rayhanah bint Sham'un An-Nadariyyah, and Mariyah Al-Qibtiyyah, the mother of his son Ibrahim; and they were among his concubines.**

Scholars including Muhammad bin Ka'b, 'Umar bin Al-Hakam, and 'Abdullah bin 'Ubaydah enumerated the Prophet's marriages, including **the two captives: Safiyyah bint Huyayy bin Akhtab, and Juwayriyah bint Al-Harith bin 'Amr bin Al-Mustaliq Al-Khuza'iyyah.**

Regarding Allah's statement: **{We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives and what their right (hands) own}**, Ubayy bin Ka'b, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir explained **it means: "Regarding limiting them to four free women and whatever concubines they wish, and stipulating the conditions of a guardian, a *Mahr*, and witnesses for them—meaning the *Ummah* (the Muslim nation). But We have granted you an exception in that, so We did not make any of that obligatory upon you, so that there may be no blame on you. God is forgiving, compassionate."**

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's address to the Prophet: *{O Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have granted their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you as spoils of war...}* (33:50), Imam al-Tabari elucidates the operative rulings:

Regarding *{their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you}*, Imam al-Tabari states: **"And We have made lawful for you your female slaves whom you have taken as captives, and thus owned them through captivity, and who have become yours due to the conquests God bestowed upon you as spoils of war."**

Regarding the distinction between the Prophet and the believers in *{exclusively for you, apart from the believers}*, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"It is mentioned that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, before this verse was revealed to him, could marry whichever women he wished. Then God restricted him to these, so he did not exceed them, and He restricted the rest of his nation to two, three, and four."**

Regarding *{We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives}*, Imam al-Tabari states: **"We know what We have made obligatory upon the believers concerning their wives if they wish to marry them, from that which We have not made obligatory upon you, and the rulings We have specified for them regarding that to your exclusion. This is that We have made it obligatory for them that a marriage contract with a free Muslim woman is not lawful except with a paternal guardian (wali 'asabah) and just witnesses, and it is not lawful for them to have more than four of them."**

Qatadah affirmed this distinction: **"It was part of what God made obligatory upon them that a woman is not married except with a guardian and a dowry in the presence of two just witnesses, and not more than four women are lawful to them, [in addition to] what their right hands possess."**

Regarding *{and what their right (hands) own}*, Imam al-Tabari delivers the legal ruling for believers: **"We know what We have made obligatory for the believers concerning their wives, because it is not lawful for them to have more than four of them, and what their right hands possess. For all of them, if they are believing women or women of the Book, are lawful to them through captivity, concubinage, and other methods of ownership."**

verses.theme: Concubinage, War Captives & Right-Hand Possession (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you, nor (is it permitted to you) to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you, except for what your right (hand) owns. God is watching over everything.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Prohibits the Prophet from marrying additional free wives or exchanging existing ones, while explicitly exempting female slave concubines. Confirms that marital caps and restrictions governing free wives never applied to the acquisition of slave chattel.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Restrictions on Additional Marriages and the Unrestricted Exemption for Concubines

Scholars including Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari stated that this Ayah was revealed as an honor and reward to the wives of the Prophet for choosing Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter when given the choice. **When they chose the Messenger of Allah, their reward was that Allah restricted him to them, and forbade him to marry anyone else or to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleased him, with the exception of female slaves and concubines, regarding whom there was no restriction.** **Then Allah lifted the restriction on him in that regard and abrogated the prohibition, permitting him to marry, but he did not marry any other women after that, so that the favor of the Messenger of Allah upon them would remain.**

Other commentators explained that Allah's statement: **{Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you}** **means: beyond the lawful categories previously specified—wives who were paid their dowries, those whom your right hand possesses from captives**, cousin emigrants, and the woman who offers herself; all categories outside of these were made unlawful to him.

Ibn 'Abbas explained: "The Messenger of Allah was forbidden from certain categories of women, except the believing emigrant women, by His saying: **{Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you, nor to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you, except for what your right (hand) owns.}** **So Allah made lawful for him believing slave girls and {a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet}**, while making unlawful women outside these categories."

Regarding His statement: **{nor to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you}**, **it means He forbade him from adding to them, or divorcing one of them and exchanging her for another, except for what his right hand possesses of female slaves, for which there was no restriction.**

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's statement: *{Beyond (that) women are not permitted to you, nor (is it permitted to you) to take (other) wives in exchange for them, even though their beauty pleases you, except for what your right (hand) owns. God is watching over everything}* (33:52), Imam al-Tabari presents the authoritative interpretation:

**"The meaning of that is: Women are not permitted to you after—after those whom I have permitted to you by My saying {Indeed We have permitted to you your wives to whom you have given their compensations...} until His saying {and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet}."**

He further explains that the verse specifically details: **"his wives, what his right hand owns that God returns to him, the daughters of his paternal uncle and his paternal aunts, the daughters of his maternal uncle and his maternal aunts who emigrated with him, and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet, making the disbelieving women specifically forbidden—then what we have said regarding that is established as correct, to the exclusion of the statement of the one who opposed our statement regarding it."**

Analyzing the syntactic structure and the explicit exception granted for female slaves, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"And {except} in His saying {except for what your right (hand) owns} is an exception from 'women'. And the meaning of that is: Women are not permitted to you after those whom I have permitted to you except what your right hand owns of slave girls, for you have the right to own slave girls from whichever of the races of people you wish."**

verses.key_legal_rulings: Codifies chastity as a core religious duty while maintaining an explicit exemption for wives and owned female slaves. Formally classifies sexual access to slave concubines as lawful alongside legal marriage, free of moral or religious blame.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
### Guarding the Private Parts Except with Wives and Female Slaves

Regarding Allah's statement: **{And who guard their private parts}** [70:29], **it means: they keep their private parts away from that which is forbidden, and prevent them from being placed in anything other than what Allah has allowed.**

This is why Allah says: **{Except concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own—surely then they are not (to be) blamed}** [70:30], **meaning: except with their wives or their female slave concubines, for in those relations they are not blameworthy.**

tafsir_tabari.text:
Regarding Allah's statement describing the righteous: *{and who guard their private parts, except concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own – surely then they are not (to be) blamed}* (70:29-30), Imam al-Tabari explains:

Regarding *{and who guard their private parts}*, he states: **"meaning: they guard their front parts from everything that Allah has forbidden them to place them in."**

Regarding the lawful exception, Imam al-Tabari explains: **"Except that they are not blameworthy in leaving their guarding, concerning their wives or what their right (hands) own of their female slaves."**

Analyzing the linguistic nuance of the text, he clarifies that although no explicit negative particle precedes the exception, the subsequent clause **"surely then they are not (to be) blamed"** indicates an implied negation in the construction. This is analogous in Arabic to saying: 'Do what seems fit to you except committing disobedience, for you will be punished for it,' with the understood meaning being: 'Do what seems fit to you, except that you will be punished for committing disobedience.'

verses.theme: Slavery as Chattel Property & Master's Maintenance Duties
verses.droge_translation: Serve God, and do not associate anything with Him, and (do) good to parents and to family, and the orphans and the poor, and the neighbor who is related and the neighbor who is a stranger, and the companion at your side, and the traveler, and what your right (hands) own. Surely God does not love anyone who is arrogant (and) boastful,
verses.key_legal_rulings: Legislates benevolence and maintenance toward owned slaves as household dependents under master jurisdiction. Establishes legal duties for owners to provide food, shelter, and appropriate workloads, reflecting the master's comprehensive property rights over chattel.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Regarding Allah's command: *{and what your right (hands) own}* (4:36), **this is an order to be kind to slaves, because the slave is weak and helpless, held as a captive in the hands of people.**

Because of this, an authentic Hadith records that during the illness that preceded his death, the Messenger of Allah continued advising his Ummah: **"(Protect) the prayer, (protect) the prayer, and (those slaves) what your right hands possess."** He repeated it continuously until his tongue could no longer speak it.

Al-Miqdam bin Ma'dikarib narrated that the Messenger of Allah said: **"What you feed yourself is a Sadaqah (charity) for you, what you feed your children is Sadaqah for you, what you feed your wife is Sadaqah for you, and what you feed your servant is Sadaqah for you."** (Recorded by Ahmad and An-Nasa'i with an authentic chain).

'Abdullah bin 'Amr asked his caretaker, "Did you give the slaves their food yet?" When he answered no, Ibn 'Amr instructed: "Go and give it to them, for the Messenger of Allah said: **'It is enough sin for someone to prevent whomever he is responsible for from getting their food.'**" (Recorded by Muslim).

Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet said: **"The slave has the right to have food and clothing, and is only required to perform what he can bear of work."** (Recorded by Muslim). Abu Hurayrah also narrated that the Prophet said: **"When your servant brings meals to one of you, if he does not let him sit with him, then he should hand him a mouthful or two mouthfuls, or a meal or two, for he managed its heat and preparation."** (Recorded in the Two Sahihs; Muslim's wording adds: "let him seat him with him to eat, and if the food is a small amount, let him place in his hand a meal or two").

Abu Dharr narrated that the Prophet said: **"They are your brothers and your servants whom Allah has placed under your hands. Whoever has his brother under his hand, he should feed him from what he eats, and clothe him from what he wears, and do not burden them with what overcomes them; and if you burden them, then help them."** (Recorded in the Two Sahihs).

tafsir_tabari.text:
### Interpretation of "What Your Right Hands Own"

Regarding the interpretation of His statement: **{and what your right (hands) own}**, Abu Ja'far al-Tabari explains: By that, He, may His praise be exalted, means: **And those whom you possess from your slaves.** Thus He attributed possession to the "right hand," just as it is said: "your mouth spoke," "your foot walked," and "your hand grasped," meaning: you spoke, you walked, and you grasped.

However, as for what each limb is described with from that, it is only attributed to that limb because the action happens through it, according to what is mutually known among people, exclusive from the rest of the body's faculties. Thus it becomes known—by describing that limb with what it was described with—what meaning is intended from the speech.

The same applies to His statement: **{and what your right (hands) own}**, because **the slaves belonging to any of us are under his hands, and they only eat what our right hands hand over, and wear what they clothe them with, and you direct them in whatever you love to direct them in with it.** So their possession is attributed to the "right hands" for that reason.

Mujahid commented regarding *{and what your right (hands) own}*: "From what God has bestowed upon you. All of this, God has enjoined."

Abu Ja'far al-Tabari explains: Mujahid only means by his saying, "All of this, God has enjoined," the parents, the relatives of kinship, the orphans, the poor, the neighbor who is related, the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion at your side, and the traveler. **Thus our Lord, Exalted is His Majesty, enjoined His servants to do good towards all of these, and commanded His creation to preserve His directive regarding them.** Therefore, it is a duty upon His servants to preserve the directive of God regarding them, and then to preserve the directive of His Messenger, may God's peace and blessings be upon him.

### The Condemnation of the Arrogant and Boastful Master

Regarding the interpretation of His statement: **{Surely God does not love anyone who is arrogant (and) boastful}** (36), Abu Ja'far al-Tabari explains: He means by His statement, may His praise be exalted, that God does not love anyone who possesses conceit (*khuyala'*). The term *al-mukhtal* (the arrogant) is derived from *khala*, meaning one who acts with arrogance and conceit (*khawlan wa-khalan*), as the poet said: "So if you are our master, you have ruled us; and if you are meant for conceit, then go away and be conceited." And Al-'Ajjaj said: "And conceit (*al-khal*) is a garment from among the garments of the ignorant ones."

As for *al-fakhur* (the boastful), it is the one who boasts over the servants of God with what God has bestowed upon him of His favors and expanded for him of His bounty, without praising Him for what He gave him of His limitless grace. Rather, he acts arrogantly and haughtily because of it, behaving overbearingly and boastfully towards others.

Mujahid explained regarding *{Surely God does not love anyone who is arrogant}* that it means "proud," and *{boastful}* means "enumerating what he has been given, while he does not thank God."

'Abdullah bin Waqid Abu Raja' al-Harawi stated: **"You do not find an evil master or an abuser of authority over slaves except that you find him arrogant and boastful."** And he recited: **{and what your right (hands) own. Surely God does not love anyone who is arrogant (and) boastful}**, adding: "Nor do you find someone persistently disobedient to parents except that you find him arrogant and deprived," reciting: **{and (made me) dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me arrogant, deprived}** (Maryam: 32).

verses.theme: Naturalized Slave Inequality & The Master-Slave Theological Parable
verses.droge_translation: God has favored some of you over others in the (matter of) provision, but those who have been favored do not give over their provision to what their right (hands) own, so (that) they are (all) equal in that respect. Is it the blessing of God they deny?
verses.key_legal_rulings: Employs the socio-economic inequality between masters and chattel as a theological argument against polytheism. Affirms that masters categorically refuse to share their wealth, beds, or estates equally with slaves, reinforcing the established master-chattel hierarchy.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Regarding Allah's statement: *{God has favored some of you over others in the (matter of) provision, but those who have been favored do not give over their provision to what their right (hands) own, so (that) they are (all) equal in that respect. Is it the blessing of God they deny?}* (16:71).

Allah points out to the idolaters their ignorance and disbelief in claiming partners alongside Allah while acknowledging that these partners are His created slaves. In their *Talbiyah* during Hajj, the pagans used to chant: "Here I am at Your service, You have no partner, except a partner that You have; You own him and whatever he owns."

So Allah Almighty said, denouncing them: **"You would not be pleased to share what We have provided you with your slaves as equals, so how could He, the Exalted, be pleased with equalizing His slaves with Him in divinity and glorification?"** This is similar to what He said in another Ayah: *{He sets forth for you a parable from your own selves: Do you have partners among those whom your right hands possess to share as equals in the wealth We have bestowed on you, whom you fear as you fear each other?}* (30:28).

Ibn 'Abbas explained concerning this Ayah: **"He says: They would never share their wealth and women with their slaves, so how could they associate My slaves with Me in My authority? That is His saying: {Is it the blessing of God they deny?}"** In another narration from him, Ibn 'Abbas said: "How can you be pleased for Me what you are not pleased for yourselves?"

Mujahid stated: "This is a parable for the false deities."

Qatadah explained: **"This is a parable set forth by Allah. Would any of you share his wife and his bed with his slave, such that you equalize Allah's creation and slaves with Allah? If you would not be pleased with this for yourself, then Allah is more deserving to be declared free from this than you."**

tafsir_tabari.text:
### The Parable of the Owned Slaves and Divine Sovereignty

He whose mention is exalted says: And God, O people, has favored some of you over others in the provision which He has provided for you in the world. But those who have been favored by God over others with what He provided for them **(do not give over their provision to what their right [hands] own)**, meaning: **they do not make their owned slaves partners in what He provided for them of wealth and spouses**, **(so [that] they are [all] equal in that respect)**, meaning: **such that they and their slaves are equal in that.**

He whose mention is exalted says: **"So they are not content that they and their owned slaves be equal in what I have provided them, yet they have made My slaves My partners in My dominion and My sovereignty."** And this is a parable that God, whose mention is exalted, struck for those who associate partners with God.

It was also said: He specifically meant by that those among the Christians who said: "The Messiah is the son of God."

Regarding His saying: **(Is it the blessing of God they deny?)**, He whose mention is exalted says: Is it the blessing of God which He bestowed upon these polytheists—of the provision which He provided for them in the world—that they deny by associating other than God from His creation as partners in His sovereignty and His dominion?

### Scholarly Interpretations of the Parable

Ibn 'Abbas stated regarding His saying, *(God has favored some of you over others in the [matter of] provision, but those who have been favored do not give over their provision to what their right [hands] own)*: **"They do not make their slaves partners in their wealth and their women, so how do they make My slaves partners with Me in My sovereignty?"** That is the meaning of His saying: *(Is it the blessing of God they deny?)*.

Ibn 'Abbas also stated: This verse was revealed regarding the matter of 'Isa the son of Maryam, meaning by that Himself. Indeed 'Isa is a slave of God, so God says: **"By God, you do not make your slaves partners in that which is yours, such that you and they become equal, so how do you accept for Me what you do not accept for yourselves?"**

Mujahid explained regarding His saying, *(do not give over their provision to what their right [hands] own)*: "It is a parable of the deities of falsehood with God, whose mention is exalted."

Qatadah explained regarding the verse: This is a parable that God struck: **"Is there anyone among you who shares his owned slave in his wife and in his bed, that you equate with God His creation and His slaves? So if you do not accept this for yourself, then God is more entitled to be declared free from it than yourself."** Therefore, do not equate anyone from His slaves and His creation with God.

Qatadah also explained: **"This is the one who has been favored in wealth and children; he does not make his slave a partner in his wealth and his wife."** He says: You have accepted that for God but did not accept it for yourself, so you made a partner for God in His dominion and His creation.

verses.theme: Total Incapacity of Owned Chattel ('Abd Mamluk) as Theological Parable
verses.droge_translation: God strikes a parable: a slave (who is) owned – he has no power over anything – and (another) whom We have provided with a good provision from Us, and he contributes from it in secret and in public. Are they equal? Praise (be) to God! No! But most of them do not know (it).
verses.key_legal_rulings: Establishes the foundational legal definition of chattel slavery: an owned slave possesses no legal capacity, property rights, or financial agency ('la yaqdiru 'ala shay'). The verse leverages this complete lack of autonomy as a theological parable.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Allah strikes a parable: *{God strikes a parable: a slave (who is) owned – he has no power over anything – and (another) whom We have provided with a good provision from Us, and he contributes from it in secret and in public. Are they equal? Praise (be) to God! No! But most of them do not know (it).}* (16:75).

Ibn 'Abbas explained: "This is a parable that Allah struck for the disbeliever and the believer." This was also stated by Qatadah, and preferred by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. **The owned slave who has no power over anything is the example of the disbeliever, and the one who is provided a good provision from which he spends secretly and openly is the believer.**

Mujahid explained: **"It is a parable struck for the idol and for the True God, Exalted be He. So are they equal?"**

And since the difference between them is plain, clear, and apparent, unknown to none but every foolish person, Allah the Exalted said: *{Praise (be) to God! No! But most of them do not know (it).}*

tafsir_tabari.text:
### The Parable of the Owned Slave and the Free Man

He, whose remembrance is exalted, says: And He has set forth a similitude for you, O people, for the disbeliever among His slaves, and the believer in Him among them.

As for the parable of the disbeliever: he does not act in obedience to God, nor does he bring any good, nor does he contribute his wealth in anything of the way of God due to the dominance of God's abandonment over him, **like the owned slave, who has no power over anything to contribute from it.**

As for the believer in God, he acts in obedience to God, and contributes his wealth in His way **like the free man whom God has given wealth, so he contributes from it in secret and in public**, meaning with the knowledge of people and without their knowledge.

### The Impossibility of Their Equality

Concerning His statement, *(Are they equal?)*, He says: **Is the slave who owns nothing and has no power over anything equal to this free man whom God has provided with a good provision so that he contributes as He described?** Thus similarly, the disbeliever acting in disobedience to God and opposing His command, and the believer acting in obedience to Him, are not equal.

### Scholarly Interpretations

Qatadah explained regarding His statement, *(God strikes a parable: a slave (who is) owned – he has no power over anything)*: This is a parable God struck for the disbeliever. He provided him with wealth but he did not put forth any good therein, nor did he act in obedience to God with it. And regarding His statement, *(and (another) whom We have provided with a good provision from Us)*: This is the believer to whom God gave wealth, so he acted in obedience to God with it, took to gratitude, and acknowledged the right of God; so God rewarded him for what He provided him with continuous, everlasting provision in Paradise. God, whose remembrance is exalted, said: **"(Are the two of them equal as a parable?) By God, they are not equal."** *(Praise (be) to God! No! But most of them do not know (it).)*.

Qatadah also stated regarding *(a slave (who is) owned – he has no power over anything)*: **"He is the disbeliever who does not act in obedience to God and does not contribute any good."** And regarding *(and (another) whom We have provided with a good provision from Us)*: **"The believer who obeys God regarding himself and his wealth."**

Ibn 'Abbas stated regarding His statement, *(God strikes a parable: a slave (who is) owned – he has no power over anything)*: **"This refers to the disbeliever, in that he is not able to make a contribution in the way of God."** And regarding *(and (another) whom We have provided with a good provision from Us, and he contributes from it in secret and in public)*: "This means the believer, and this parable is regarding spending and contribution."

Regarding His statement, *(Praise (be) to God!)*, He says: Complete praise is for God purely, to the exclusion of what you invoke besides Him of the idols. So Him alone should you praise, to their exclusion. And His statement, *(No! But most of them do not know (it))* means: The matter is not as you do, nor is the saying as you say. The idols do not possess any favor or good deed for which they can be praised; praise belongs only to God. But most of these disbelievers who worship them do not know that this is so; thus, out of their ignorance, they make them partners with God in worship and praise.

Mujahid stated: **"God struck this parable, and the other parable after it, for Himself and the deities that are worshipped besides Him."**

verses.theme: Modesty Boundaries & Veiling Exceptions for Owned Slaves (Milk al-Yamin)
verses.droge_translation: And say to the believing women (that) they (should) lower their sight and guard their private parts, and not show their charms, except for what (normally) appears of them. And let them draw their head coverings over their breasts, and not show their charms, except to their husbands, or their fathers, or their husbands’ fathers, or their sons, or their husbands’ sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons, or their women, or what their right (hands) own, or such men as attend (them who) have no (sexual) desire, or children (who are) not (yet) aware of women’s nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they hide of their charms. Turn to God (in repentance) – all (of you) – believers, so that you may prosper.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Exempts 'what their right hands own' from strict hijab and veiling requirements before free women alongside blood mahrams. Classical jurisprudence permitted female owners to uncover hair and limbs before domestic slaves due to their legal chattel status.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Allah commands: *{And say to the believing women (that) they (should) lower their sight and guard their private parts, and not show their charms, except for what (normally) appears of them. And let them draw their head coverings over their breasts, and not show their charms, except to their husbands, or their fathers, or their husbands’ fathers, or their sons, or their husbands’ sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons, or their women, or what their right (hands) own, or such men as attend (them who) have no (sexual) desire, or children (who are) not (yet) aware of women’s nakedness...}* (24:31).

Regarding the exception: *{or what their right (hands) own}*:

Ibn Jurayj said: **"This means from among the women of the polytheists. It is permissible for a Muslim woman to reveal her adornment to her even if she is a polytheist, because she is her slave-girl."** This was also the view of Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib.

**The majority of scholars held: "Rather, it is permissible for her to reveal it to her slaves, both men and women."** They cited as evidence the Hadith recorded by Abu Dawud from Anas: The Prophet brought Fatimah a slave he had gifted to her. Fatimah was wearing a garment which, if she covered her head with it, did not reach her feet, and if she covered her feet with it, did not reach her head. When the Prophet saw what she was struggling with, he said: **"There is no harm upon you; it is only your father and your boy (slave)."**

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in his history, in the biography of Hudayj the eunuch (the freed slave of Mu'awiyah), that 'Abdullah bin Mas'adah Al-Fazari was intensely dark-skinned, and that the Prophet had gifted him to his daughter Fatimah. She raised him and then freed him, and after all that, he was with Mu'awiyah during the days of Siffin, being among the fiercest opponents against 'Ali bin Abi Talib.

Umm Salamah narrated that the Messenger of Allah said: **"If any of you women has a Mukatib (a slave who has contracted to buy his freedom), and he has the means to pay, she must observe Hijab from him."** (Recorded by Ahmad and Abu Dawud).

tafsir_tabari.text:
### The Meaning of "Or Their Women"

Regarding the interpretation of His saying, *{or their women}*, Ibn Jurayj stated: **"It reached me that they are the women of the Muslims; it is not lawful for a Muslim woman that a polytheist woman sees her nakedness, unless she is a slave girl belonging to her, and that is His saying: {or what their right (hands) own}."**

'Ubadah bin Nusayy reported that he disliked that a Christian woman should kiss a Muslim woman or see her nakedness, interpreting *{or their women}* as referring strictly to Muslim women. 'Umar bin al-Khattab wrote to Abu 'Ubaydah bin al-Jarrah: "To proceed, it has reached me that women enter the public baths, and with them are women of the People of the Book. So prevent that, and stand in the way of it." Abu 'Ubaydah then stood up and supplicated intensely: "O Allah, whichever woman enters the bath without illness or sickness, seeking whiteness for her face, then blacken her face on the Day when faces will become white."

### The Meaning of "Or What Their Right Hands Own"

Regarding His saying, *{or what their right (hands) own}*, the scholars of interpretation differed.

**Some of them said: This refers to their owned slaves (mamalik), for there is no harm upon a woman to show them of her charm what she shows to these specified relatives and women.** In the earlier recitation according to Makhlad at-Tamimi from 'Amr bin Dinar, it was recited as: "what your right hands own" (*aymanukum*).

**And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: or what their right hands own of the female slaves of the polytheists. Just as Ibn Jurayj mentioned previously, when Allah said *{or their women}*, He meant by them the Muslim women, excluding polytheist women. Then He added: *{or what their right (hands) own}*, referring specifically to their non-Muslim female slaves.**

verses.theme: Master's Legal Jurisdiction & Command over Slave Marriages
verses.droge_translation: Marry off the unmarried among you, and (also) the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves. If they are poor, God will enrich them from His favor. God is embracing, knowing.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Commands masters to arrange marriages for male and female slaves. Establishes that enslaved individuals lack autonomous legal agency to contract their own marriages, placing matrimonial authority entirely under the master's ownership rights.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Allah commands: *{Marry off the unmarried among you, and (also) the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves. If they are poor, God will enrich them from His favor. God is embracing, knowing.}* (24:32).

These clear Ayat include a group of unambiguous rulings and firm commands. His saying: *{And marry off the unmarried (Al-Ayama) among you, and (also) the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves}* **is a command to marry.** A group of scholars held that marriage is obligatory upon anyone capable of it, relying upon the apparent meaning of the Prophet's statement: "O young men, whoever among you can afford to get married, let him marry, for it is more effective in lowering the gaze and protecting the private parts. Whoever cannot do that, then let him fast, for it is a protection for him." (Recorded in the Two Sahihs from Ibn Mas'ud).

*Al-Ayama* is the plural of *Ayyim*, referring to a woman without a husband and a man without a wife, whether previously married and separated or never married at all.

Regarding Allah's promise: *{If they are poor, God will enrich them from His favor. God is embracing, knowing}*, Ibn 'Abbas explained: **"Allah encouraged them to marry, and commanded both the free and the slaves to do so, promising them wealth for it, saying: {If they are poor, God will enrich them from His favor}."**

Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah said: **"There are three whom it is a right upon Allah to help: one who gets married seeking chastity; a slave who makes a contract with his master with the aim of buying his freedom (Mukatab); and one who fights for the sake of Allah."** (Recorded by Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah).

tafsir_tabari.text:
### Linguistic Meaning of Al-Ayama (The Unmarried) and the Command to Marry Slaves

He, whose mention is exalted, says: **"Marry off, O believers, those who have no spouse from among your free men and women, and from the people of righteousness among your male slaves and your bondsmen."**

The word *al-ayama* (the unmarried) is the plural of *ayyim*. It takes the pattern of *fa'ilah*, pluralized as *ayama* just as *yatimah* (female orphan) is pluralized as *yatama* (orphans). The term *ayyim* applies to both male and female; it is said of a man that he is *ayyim* and of a woman that she is *ayyim* or *ayyimah* when they have no spouse. Jamil al-'Udhri said: "I love the unmarried women (*ayama*) when Buthaynah is an unmarried woman (*ayyim*), and I loved, when you became satisfied with marriage, the married women (*ghawani*)." And another poet recited: "If you marry, I will marry, and if you remain unmarried (*tata'ayyami*), even if I am younger than you all, I will remain unmarried (*ata'ayyamu*)." Thus *ayyim* in the Mighty Revelation includes both male and female, virgin and previously married.

### Exegesis of "If They Are Poor, God Will Enrich Them"

Regarding His statement, **{If they are poor}**, He says: **If these whom you marry off—from among the unmarried of your free men and women, and your male and female slaves—are people of need and poverty, then Allah will enrich them from His favor, so do not let their poverty prevent you from marrying them off.**

Ibn 'Abbas stated regarding His saying, **{Marry off the unmarried among you, and (also) the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves}**: **"Allah, the Exalted, commanded marriage, encouraged them towards it, and commanded them to marry off their free men and their slaves, promising them enrichment in that, saying: {If they are poor, God will enrich them from His favor}."**

'Abdullah bin Mas'ud said: "Seek wealth in marriage; Allah says: **{If they are poor, God will enrich them from His favor}**."

Ibn Zayd explained regarding His saying, *{Marry off the unmarried among you}*: "The unmarried among women (*ayama al-nisa'*): those who do not have husbands."

### Divine Grace and Knowledge

Regarding His saying, **{God is embracing, knowing}**, He whose praise is glorious says: Allah is embracing in favor, generous in His gifts. **So marry off your female slaves, for Allah is embracing; He expands His provision upon them from His favor if they are poor.** Regarding **{knowing}**, He says: He is the Possessor of knowledge regarding the poor and the rich among them; the condition and management of His creation are never hidden from Him.

verses.theme: The Contract of Mukataba & Prohibition of Coerced Slave Prostitution
verses.droge_translation: Let those who do not find (the means for) marriage abstain, until God enriches them from His favor. Those who seek the writ, among what your right (hands) own, write (it) for them, if you know any good in them, and give them some of the wealth of God which He has given you. And do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish (to live in) chastity, so that you may seek (the fleeting) goods of this present life. Whoever forces them – surely God is forgiving (and) compassionate (to them) after their being forced.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Institutes the contract of manumission through purchase (mukataba) and commands financial aid for contracting slaves. Explicitly prohibits masters from coercing female slaves into prostitution for commercial profit while confirming divine forgiveness for the coerced women.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Allah says: *{Let those who do not find (the means for) marriage abstain, until God enriches them from His favor. Those who seek the writ, among what your right (hands) own, write (it) for them, if you know any good in them, and give them some of the wealth of God which He has given you. And do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish (to live in) chastity, so that you may seek (the fleeting) goods of this present life. Whoever forces them – surely God is forgiving (and) compassionate (to them) after their being forced.}* (24:33).

This Ayah is general, whereas the verse in Surat An-Nisa' is more specific: *{And whoever of you have not the means wherewith to wed free believing women, they may wed believing girls from among those whom your right hands possess... This is for him among you who is in fear of sin. And to be patient is better for you}* (4:25)—**meaning, your patience in refraining from marrying slave-girls is better, because the child born to them will also be a slave.**

Regarding Allah's command: *{Those who seek the writ, among what your right (hands) own, write (it) for them, if you know any good in them}*: **This is a command from Allah to slave-owners: if their servants ask them for a contract of emancipation (Kitabah), they should write it for them, provided that the servant has a skill and means of earning so that he can pay his master the agreed-upon sum.** Many scholars view this command as recommendation and guidance rather than strict legal obligation. Under this view, the master retains the choice: if he wishes he writes it, and if he wishes he does not. Ash-Sha'bi, 'Ata' bin Abi Rabah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri all stated: "If he wishes he writes it for him, and if he does not wish he does not."

**Other scholars held that it is legally obligatory upon the master to grant the contract if the servant requests it, taking the apparent meaning of the command.** 'Ata' stated: "I do not think it can be anything but obligatory." Musa bin Anas narrated that **Sirin asked Anas bin Malik for a contract of emancipation—and Sirin possessed substantial wealth—but Anas refused. Sirin went to 'Umar bin Al-Khattab, who ordered Anas: "Write it for him." When Anas still refused, 'Umar struck him with a whip and recited: *{write (it) for them, if you know any good in them}*, whereupon Anas wrote the contract.** (Recorded by Al-Bukhari, 'Abdur-Razzaq, and Ibn Jarir with an authentic chain). Ad-Dahhak likewise ruled: "It is an absolute obligation." This was the earlier position of Imam Ash-Shafi'i. **However, in his later school of jurisprudence, Ash-Shafi'i concluded it is not obligatory, citing the Prophet's Hadith: "The property of a Muslim is not lawful except with his willing consent."**

Imam Malik stated: **"The established ruling among us is that the master of a slave is not obligated to write a contract of emancipation for him if he asks for that, and I have not heard of any Imam compelling anyone to write a contract of emancipation for his slave. Rather, it is a command of permission and guidance from Allah, not an obligation."** This was also the view of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, and 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam. **However, Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari favored the view of legal obligation due to the apparent command of the Ayah.**

Regarding the condition *{if you know any good in them}*, commentators explained "good" as trustworthiness, honesty, wealth, or earning capability. Yahya bin Abi Kathir reported that the Prophet said regarding this verse: **"If you know them to have a profession, and do not let them loose to be a burden on the people."** (Recorded by Abu Dawud in *Al-Marasil*).

Regarding Allah's command: *{and give them some of the wealth of God which He has given you}*, the exegetes differed. **Some held that it means: deduct a portion of the emancipation contract price for them—such as a quarter, a third, a half, or an agreed portion.** Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata', Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazzah, 'Abd Al-Karim Al-Jazari, and As-Suddi stated: **"Meaning: Deduct for them from their contracts of emancipation."** **Others held that it refers to allocating the share of obligatory Zakah that Allah established for freeing slaves.** This was the view of Al-Hasan, Zayd bin Aslam, 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd, and Muqatil, and was favored by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, Buraydah, and Qatadah explained that Allah urged the master and the broader community to assist the slave financially. Ibn 'Abbas stated: "Allah commanded the believers to help in freeing slaves," in accordance with the Prophet's Hadith: **"There are three whom it is a right upon Allah to help: [including] the slave who contracts with his master seeking to pay it off."**

Regarding the prohibition: *{And do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish (to live in) chastity, so that you may seek (the fleeting) goods of this present life}*: **In pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah, when a man owned a slave-girl, he would send her out to commit Zina and levy a recurring tax upon her earnings. When Islam came, Allah strictly prohibited Muslims from doing that.**

**Exegetes record that this Ayah was revealed concerning 'Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, the leader of the hypocrites, who forced his slave-girls into prostitution to take their earnings, seek offspring, and gain status.** Jabir narrated: **"This was revealed about a slave-girl belonging to 'Abdullah bin Ubayy named Musaykah. He used to force her to commit immoral acts—though there was no fault in her—but she refused. Then Allah revealed this Ayah up to: *{Whoever forces them – surely God is forgiving (and) compassionate (to them) after their being forced}*."** As-Suddi reported: **"'Abdullah bin Ubayy had a slave-girl called Mu'adhah, and whenever a guest came, he would send her to him for intercourse, desiring reward and honor. The slave-girl complained to Abu Bakr, who informed the Prophet. The Prophet ordered her taken away, prompting 'Abdullah bin Ubayy to cry: 'Who will excuse me from Muhammad, who overpowers us over our property?' So Allah revealed this verse."**

Regarding *{Whoever forces them – surely God is forgiving (and) compassionate (to them) after their being forced}*: **This divine forgiveness and mercy applies specifically to the compelled slave-girls, while the sin and guilt fall entirely upon the master who forced them.** Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata' Al-Khurasani, Al-A'mash, and Qatadah confirmed this. Al-Hasan exclaimed: **"To them, by Allah! To them, by Allah!"** Az-Zuhri said: **"Forgiving to them for what they were forced into."** Zayd bin Aslam affirmed: **"Forgiving, Most Merciful to the women who were forced."** This is corroborated by the Prophet's Hadith: **"My Ummah is excused for mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are forced to do."**

tafsir_tabari.text:
### The Contract of Emancipation (Mukatabah)

Regarding His statement, *{Those who seek the writ, among what your right (hands) own}*, He, glorified be His praise, says: And those who seek the contract of emancipation (*mukatabah*) from you among your slaves, *{write (it) for them, if you know any good in them}*.

The scholars of interpretation differed regarding whether a master writing a contract of emancipation for a qualified slave is an obligation (*fard*) or a recommendation (*nadb*).

**Some scholars stated: It is an obligation upon a master to write a contract of emancipation for his slave in whom he knows there is good, if the slave requests that of him.**

Ibn Jurayj reported: "I said to 'Ata': 'Is it obligatory upon me, if I know he has wealth, that I write a contract of emancipation for him?' He said: **'I do not see it as anything but obligatory.'** And 'Amr bin Dinar held the same view."

Anas bin Malik reported that his slave Sirin asked him to write a contract of emancipation for him, but Anas delayed and hesitated, whereupon 'Umar bin al-Khattab told him: **"You shall certainly write him a contract of emancipation."**

Ibn 'Abbas stated: **"It is not appropriate for a man, if he has a righteous slave who has wealth and wants to enter into a contract of emancipation, that he does not write a contract of emancipation for him."**

**Other scholars held: That is not obligatory upon the master; rather, His saying *{write (it) for them}* is a recommendation from Allah to slave-owners to write an emancipation contract for whoever among them in whom good is known, not a binding obligation.**

Malik bin Anas stated: **"The established practice according to us is that it is not obligatory upon the master of the slave to write a contract of emancipation for him if he asks him for that, and I have not heard of anyone among the Imams who forced anyone to write a contract of emancipation for his slave."** Malik added: "This is merely a command which Allah permitted for the people; it is not an obligation upon them, nor is it binding upon anyone." Sufyan al-Thawri likewise stated: "If the slave wants his master to write a contract of emancipation for him, the master may do so if he wishes, but he is not compelled." Ibn Zayd similarly remarked: "It is not obligatory upon him to write a contract of emancipation; this is merely a permissible directive and guidance from Allah."

### Imam al-Tabari's Preferred View on the Obligation of Mukatabah

**The most correct of the two statements in this regard, in my view, is the statement of those who said: It is obligatory upon the master of the slave to write a contract of emancipation for him if he knows there is good in him and the slave requests the contract. This is because the apparent form of His saying *{write (it) for them}* is an explicit command, and the command of Allah is an obligation to be fulfilled unless there is proof from the Book or Sunnah showing it to be a recommendation, as we have explained in our work *Al-Bayan 'an Usul al-Ahkam*.**

### The Definition of "Good" (Khayr) in the Slave

The scholars differed concerning the nature of the "good" (*khayr*) required within the slave:

**First, some scholars stated: It is the ability to acquire a trade and earn a livelihood in order to fulfill what was contracted, without burdening the Muslim community.**

Ibn 'Umar disliked writing an emancipation contract for a slave who had no trade, stating: **"Would you have me feed off the dirt of the people?"**

Ibn 'Abbas explained regarding *{if you know any good in them}*: **"If you know they have a means of earning, and will not cast their burden of provision upon the Muslims."** Malik bin Anas and Zayd bin Aslam likewise stated: "The good is the strength and capacity to pay."

**Second, other scholars stated: It means honesty, fulfillment, trustworthiness, and financial capability.**

Al-Hasan al-Basri explained: **"It means honesty, fulfillment, payment, and trustworthiness."** Mujahid and Tawus held it means "wealth and trustworthiness." Abu Salih stated: "Payment and trustworthiness." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Honesty and fulfillment." 'Ata' stated: "Payment and wealth." 'Amr bin Dinar commented: "I consider it to encompass all of that: wealth and righteousness."

**Third, other scholars stated: It refers strictly to possessing wealth.**

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and 'Ata' bin Abi Rabah reported that *khayr* in this context means existing wealth, citing the verse: *{if he leaves any good}* (Al-Baqarah: 180).

### Imam al-Tabari's Synthesis on "Good"

**The most correct interpretation in my view is the view of those who said: It means write contracts of emancipation for them if you know they have the strength and ability to practice a profession and earn, along with fulfillment of what they have obligated themselves to and honesty in speech.** These attributes are what the master needs from the slave's character. As for existing wealth, although it is good, it is something external to the slave rather than residing *in* him (*fihim*). Since Allah conditioned the contract on knowing good *in* them, it refers to internal capability and integrity.

### Giving to Slaves from the Wealth of Allah

Regarding His statement, *{and give them some of the wealth of God which He has given you}*, the scholars differed regarding who is commanded and which wealth is intended:

**The first view: The command is addressed to the master to discount or remit a portion of the agreed emancipation contract price, specifically a quarter.**

'Ali ibn Abi Talib explained regarding *{and give them some of the wealth of God which He has given you}*: **"A quarter of the emancipation contract; he discounts it for him."** Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami applied this by waiving a quarter of a contract of 1,200 dirhams, noting that 'Ali did the same.

Ibn 'Abbas stated: **"Discount for them from their emancipation contracts."**

Zaynab bint Qays bin Makhramah contracted a slave for 10,000 dirhams and remitted 1,000 for him. Abu Usayd contracted his slave for 1,200 dirhams, took 1,000, and returned 200 to him. When Ibn 'Umar contracted his slave Sharaf for 35,000 dirhams, he discounted 5,000 from the final installment so as not to forfeit the charity should the slave fail early on. Malik bin Anas observed: "That a master waives a specified portion from the end of his slave's contract is the best practice I have heard, and upon this are the scholars."

**The second view: The command is an exhortation to the broader Muslim community and rulers to grant contracted slaves their designated share from the obligatory Zakah and public revenues, in accordance with Allah's decree: *{Charities are only for the poor... and for the slaves}* (At-Tawbah: 60).**

Ibn Zayd explained: **"That refers to the Zakah upon the rulers; they must give them from the Zakah, for Allah says: *{and for the slaves}*."** His father Zayd bin Aslam said: "What does the master have to do with the emancipation contract? It is from the public wealth of Allah in which a legal share has been obligated for the slave." Al-Hasan al-Basri and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i likewise stated that Allah commanded the master and all Muslims to assist the contracted slave from public funds.

### Imam al-Tabari's Preferred View on Financial Aid

**The most correct of the two statements in my view is the second: that Allah meant granting them their legal share from the obligatory charity (Zakah).** This is because Allah's command is a binding obligation upon the wealthy believers, and no one has an inherent claim upon another's private property except what Allah has obligated through the institutional shares of Zakah. Since the contract debt is the private property of the master, the divine command directs the community to allocate from God's obligatory charities to emancipate the slave.

### Prohibition of Forcing Female Slaves into Prostitution

Regarding the statement of the Exalted: **{And do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish (to live in) chastity, so that you may seek (the fleeting) goods of this present life. Whoever forces them – surely God is forgiving (and) compassionate (to them) after their being forced.}**

Abu Ja'far al-Tabari explains: **"Marry the righteous among your male and female slaves, and do not force your slave-girls into prostitution, which is fornication (*zina*); *{if they wish (to live in) chastity}* means if they desire to refrain from *zina*."**

Regarding *{so that you may seek (the fleeting) goods of this present life}*, He says: so that you may seek, by compelling them into *zina*, the material gains, earnings, and worldly goods of this life. **{Whoever forces them} means: whoever compels his slave-girls into prostitution, surely Allah, following their being coerced, is forgiving and compassionate towards them; and the burden of sin falls entirely upon the masters who forced them, exclusive of the coerced women.**

### Occasions of Revelation and Historical Context

Jabir bin 'Abdullah reported: "Musaykah, a slave-girl belonging to 'Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, was forced by her master into *zina* to earn money. She came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and complained of that, whereupon Allah revealed: *{And do not force your young women into prostitution...}*"

Al-Zuhri related: **"A man from Quraysh was taken captive on the day of Badr and held by 'Abdullah bin Ubayy. Ibn Ubayy had a slave-girl named Mu'adhah, and the captive desired her; but she was a Muslim and refused him because of her Islam. Ibn Ubayy began forcing and beating her, hoping she would bear a child for the Qurayshi captive so he could demand a heavy ransom for the child. Thereupon Allah revealed: {And do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish (to live in) chastity}."**

Al-Sha'bi, 'Ikrimah, and Mujahid noted that during the Pre-Islamic Era of Ignorance (*Jahiliyyah*), masters routinely commanded their female slaves to engage in prostitution and seized their earnings (*kasb*). When a slave-girl accepted Islam and refused this immorality, Ibn Ubayy attempted to compel her, prompting the revelation.

Ibn 'Abbas stated: **"During Jahiliyyah they used to force their female slaves into *zina* and take their wages. Allah forbade forcing them into fornication for worldly gain, and declared that if they are coerced, Allah the Exalted is forgiving and compassionate towards the women, while the sin rests entirely upon the one who forced them."**

verses.theme: Household Slave Privacy Laws & Domestic Service Circulation
verses.droge_translation: You who believe! Let those whom your right (hands) own, and those of you who have not reached the (age of) puberty, ask permission of you at three times (of the day) – before the dawn prayer, and when you lay down your clothes at the noon hour, and after the evening prayer – the three (times) of nakedness for you. But beyond those (times) there is no blame on you or on them in going about among each other. In this way God makes clear to you the signs. God is knowing, wise.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Mandates that household slaves request entry permission only during three specific times of potential unclothed privacy (dawn, midday rest, and night). Grants unrestricted domestic circulation at all other times to facilitate continuous household servitude.
