tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Allah commands: *{You who believe! Let those whom your right (hands) own, and those of you who have not reached the (age of) puberty, ask permission of you at three times (of the day) – before the dawn prayer, and when you lay down your clothes at the noon hour, and after the evening prayer – the three (times) of nakedness for you. But beyond those (times) there is no blame on you or on them in going about among each other. In this way God makes clear to you the signs. God is knowing, wise.}* (24:58).

These Ayat establish how household members and dependents must seek permission to enter upon one another. **Allah commanded the believers to ensure that their servants and prepubescent children seek permission at three designated times: before the Fajr prayer (when people are asleep in their beds), when laying down clothes at the noon hour (the time of rest, when a man may be in a state of undress with his wife), and after the Isha prayer (the hour of sleep). Servants and children are commanded not to enter upon household members at these times without permission, lest they encounter someone in an intimate situation.**

Regarding other times, Allah says: *{the three (times) of nakedness for you. But beyond those (times) there is no blame on you or on them}*. **If they enter at times other than these three, there is no sin upon household members in letting them enter, nor upon the servants if they inadvertently see something. They are permitted general entry because they circulate constantly throughout the house to provide service (At-Tawwafin), and are forgiven for incidental exposure in a way that unrelated outsiders are not.** This parallels the Prophet's ruling regarding the domestic cat: "It is not impure; it is one of those that circulate among you (*At-Tawwafin*)."

**Although this Ayah is entirely clear, decisive, and unabrogated, many people neglected acting upon it, drawing strong rebuke from the Companions.** Sa'id bin Jubayr reported that Ibn 'Abbas said: "The people have abandoned three verses and do not act upon them: *{You who believe! Let those whom your right (hands) own, and those of you who have not reached the (age of) puberty, ask permission of you at three times}* (24:58); *{And when relatives, orphans, and the poor attend the division, provide for them out of it}* (4:8); and *{Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you}* (49:13)." Ibn 'Abbas affirmed: **"Most people do not follow it—the Ayah that speaks about asking permission—but I explicitly command my servant woman to seek permission before entering upon me."** (Recorded by Abu Dawud). When Ash-Sha'bi was asked about the verse, he affirmed: **"It has not been abrogated."**

Ibn 'Abbas explained the historical context: **"Indeed Allah is Concealing and loves concealment. In the early period, people did not have curtains on their doors or canopies in their houses, so a man's servant, child, or orphan might surprise him while he was with his wife. Thus Allah commanded them to seek permission during those designated times of privacy.** Later, Allah expanded their provision and they installed curtains and canopies, leading people to assume that curtains rendered seeking permission unnecessary." (Authentic chain recorded by Abu Dawud and Ibn Abi Hatim).

As-Suddi noted: **"Some Companions used to engage in intimate relations with their wives during these hours so they could bathe before going out for prayer; thus Allah commanded them to order their slaves and boys not to enter upon them during those hours except with permission."** Muqatil bin Hayyan added that Asma' bint Murshidah said to the Prophet: **"O Messenger of Allah, how ugly this is! A servant boy might enter upon a woman and her husband while they are under one cover without permission!"** Whereupon Allah revealed this verse. The permanent authority of this rule is confirmed by the closing decree: *{In this way God makes clear to you the signs. God is knowing, wise.}*

tafsir_tabari.text:
### Scope of "Those Whom Your Right Hands Own"

Regarding His saying, *{Let those whom your right (hands) own ask permission of you}*, the scholars of interpretation differed.

Some held: **What is meant by this is male slaves excluding females; they were forbidden from entering upon their masters during these three specific times except with permission.** Ibn 'Umar stated: "It applies to males excluding females."

Others held: **Rather, what is meant by it is both male and female slaves.** Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami stated: **"It applies to men and women; they must ask permission in every circumstance, by night and by day."**

Imam al-Tabari concludes: **The more correct of the two statements in my view is that it encompasses both males and females. Allah stated generally *{those whom your right (hands) own}*, encompassing all slaves possessed by our right hands without specifying gender. Thus the interpretation is: O you who believe, let your male and female slaves seek your permission before entering upon you during these times.**

### The Three Times of Domestic Privacy

Regarding *{and those of you who have not reached the (age of) puberty}*, He means the free young children who have not attained puberty. Regarding *{three times (of the day)}*, it designates three distinct intervals during the day and night: before the dawn prayer, at the noon rest when clothing is laid aside, and after the evening (*'isha'*) prayer.

Mujahid explained *{those whom your right (hands) own}* as "your enslaved servants," and *{those of you who have not reached puberty}* as "the free children who have not reached puberty."

'Ata' bin Abi Rabah affirmed that every young boy and girl must seek permission during these three times: before dawn, at noon, and after the late evening prayer (*'atamah*) until morning. Salih bin Kaysan, Ya'qub bin 'Utbah, and Isma'il bin Muhammad concurred: "There is no obligation for a man's domestic servants to ask permission except during these three times of privacy."

Ibn 'Abbas explained: **"When a man withdraws in privacy with his wife after the 'Isha' prayer, no servant or child may enter upon him except with permission until he prays the morning prayer; and when he withdraws in privacy with his wife at the Dhuhr prayer, the same applies."**

'Abdullah bin Suwayd al-Harithi stated: "When I lay down my clothes at noon, no servant who has reached puberty nor any free child who has not reached puberty may enter upon me except with permission."

### Neglect of the Command and Ongoing Validity

Ibn 'Abbas stated: **"Three verses have been neglected by the people: the obligation of seeking permission entirely; the verse *{Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you}*, whereas people say nobility is lineage; and a third."**

Al-Hasan al-Basri noted: "If a man lodges his servant to sleep in the same room with him, that constant presence serves as his permission; but if he does not lodge him with him, the servant must seek permission during these three hours."

Ash-Sha'bi was asked about this verse: **"Is it abrogated?" He replied: "No, by Allah, it has not been abrogated!" When told that people no longer act upon it, he replied: "Allah is the one whose help is sought!"** Sa'id bin Jubayr similarly affirmed: **"Some people claim it was abrogated, but rather it is among the commands that people take lightly and fail to practice today."**

### Recitation and Rulings on Free Domestic Circulation

The reciters of Madinah and Basrah read *thalathu 'awratin* (nominative), indicating that these three specified periods are times of privacy when garments are removed and spouses retire together. The reciters of Kufa read *thalatha 'awratin* (accusative). Imam al-Tabari notes that both readings are authentic and convey convergent meanings.

Regarding His saying, *{But beyond those (times) there is no blame on you or on them in going about among each other}*, He whose mention is exalted clarifies: **There is no restriction and no sin upon masters or upon their domestic slaves and young children if they enter without permission outside of these three specified times.**

Ibn 'Abbas explained: **"Allah granted a concession for a man's servant and child to enter his dwelling without permission between the morning prayer and noon, and between noon and the evening prayer."** However, a free person who has attained puberty must seek permission at all times under every circumstance.

The phrase *{going about among each other}* (*tawwafun*) describes how domestic slaves and household members must constantly circulate in the service of the family throughout the day. In this way, Allah clarifies His legal boundaries with wisdom and complete knowledge of human welfare.

verses.theme: Denial of Shared Property & Inheritance with Slaves as Theological Parable
verses.droge_translation: He has struck a parable for you from yourselves: Among what your right (hands) own, do you have associates in what We have provided you with, so that you are (all) equal in that respect – (you) fearing them as you fear each other? In this way We make the signs distinct for a people who understand.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Refutes polytheism by citing the absolute property divide between masters and chattel. Highlights that masters would never admit slaves as equal co-owners of their wealth or fear them as equal heirs, reaffirming strict chattel inequality.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Allah says: *{He has struck a parable for you from yourselves: Among what your right (hands) own, do you have associates in what We have provided you with, so that you are (all) equal in that respect – (you) fearing them as you fear each other? In this way We make the signs distinct for a people who understand.}* (30:28).

**This is the parable Allah sets forth regarding the idolaters who worship others besides Him and attribute partners to Him, while admitting that these purported partners are His created slaves.** In their pre-Islamic *Talbiyah* during Hajj, they used to say: "At Your service, You have no partner except the partner that You have; You own him and whatever he owns."

Allah explains: *{He sets forth for you a parable from yourselves}*—meaning an example drawn from your own direct experience—*{Do you have partners among those whom your right hands possess to share as equals in the wealth We have bestowed on you}*, **meaning none of you would ever accept having his slave as an equal partner in his wealth, each having an equal share.** Regarding *{whom you fear as you fear each other}*, Abu Mijlaz explained: **"You do not fear that your servant will claim an equal share in your wealth because he has no such legal right; similarly, Allah has no partner."**

**The meaning is: since any human master vehemently abhors sharing his wealth with his slave as an equal, how can they attribute rivals and partners to Allah from among His own created servants?** This is similar to His saying: *{And they assign to Allah that which they dislike (for themselves)}* (16:62), referring to how the pagans abhorred having daughters yet blasphemously ascribed daughters and female angels to Allah. **Likewise, in this context, they assigned divine partners to Allah from among His created servants, whereas any one of them would absolutely refuse and abhor that his slave should be an equal partner in his wealth.**

Ibn 'Abbas narrated that the idolaters recited in their *Talbiyah*: "At Your service, O Allah, You have no partner except the partner that You have; You own him and whatever he owns," whereupon Allah revealed this verse to demonstrate that if humans refuse equality with their slaves, Allah is infinitely more exalted above having equal partners from His creation.

tafsir_tabari.text:
### The Parable of the Owned Associates

Regarding the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted: **{He has struck a parable for you from yourselves: Among what your right (hands) own, do you have associates in what We have provided you with, so that you are (all) equal in that respect – (you) fearing them as you fear each other? In this way We make the signs distinct for a people who understand.}** (28)

He, may His mention be exalted, says: Your Lord has struck a parable for you, O people, drawn from your own human reality. **{Among what your right (hands) own} means: Do you have among your owned slaves any partners in the wealth and provision We have granted you, such that you and they are equal co-owners in it? If you never accept such equality for yourselves with your own human slaves, how then can you attribute to Allah partners from His creation in divinity and worship, when both you and your idols are merely His created slaves and possessions, and He is the sole Sovereign Owner of all?**

Qatadah explained: **"This is a parable Allah struck for those who attribute equals to Him. Would any of you make his owned slave an equal partner in his wealth, his bed, and his wife?! If you do not accept this for yourself, then Allah is far more entitled to be declared free from having any equal among His creation."**

Ibn Zayd stated: **"Do you find anyone who places his slave on an equal footing with himself in his wealth? How then do you deliberately, while admitting that they are My slaves and My creation, assign to them a share in My exclusive worship?"**

### Interpretations of "Fearing Them as You Fear Each Other"

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of *{(you) fearing them as you fear each other}*:

Ibn 'Abbas held: **"You fear that these associates from among your slaves might inherit your wealth after your death, just as free relatives inherit from one another."**

Abu Mijlaz held: **"You do not fear that your owned slave will demand a division of your wealth with you as an equal partner, because he has no legal right to do so. Similarly, Allah has no partner in His dominion."**

### Imam al-Tabari's Preferred Interpretation

**The more correct interpretation in my view is the second: that it refers to the fear of dividing and partitioning wealth. Allah rebuked the polytheists who worship created beings while admitting they are God's slaves, asking them: Do you have among your slaves any partners in the wealth We bestowed upon you, such that you fear they will divide that shared property with you, just as you fear independent free partners dividing shared property?**

The mention of partnership (*shirkah*) naturally implies the apprehension of dividing shared property between co-owners during life, rather than the laws of inheritance.

Regarding His saying, *{In this way We make the signs distinct for a people who understand}*, He explains: Just as We have clarified Our proofs regarding Our absolute power and singular right to worship, We elucidate Our evidence for people who reflect, take heed, and understand the truth.

verses.theme: Hijab & Veiling Exemptions for Slaves of the Prophet's Wives
verses.droge_translation: (There is) no blame on them concerning their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons, or their women, or what their right (hands) own. But guard (yourselves) against God. Surely God is a witness over everything.
verses.key_legal_rulings: Exempts owned slaves alongside close male relatives from strict veiling and partition (hijab) rules before the Prophet's wives and free women. Affirms that domestic slave ownership created a practical, institutional exception to modesty boundaries.

tafsir_ibn_kathir.text:
Allah says: *{(There is) no blame on them concerning their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons, or their women, or what their right (hands) own. But guard (yourselves) against God. Surely God is a witness over everything.}* (33:55).

**When Allah commanded women to observe Hijab in front of non-mahram men, He specified the categories of relatives and household members before whom they do not need to observe Hijab.** This parallels the exemptions enumerated in Surat An-Nur: *{And not to reveal their adornment except to their husbands, or their fathers, or their husbands' fathers, or their sons, or their husbands' sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons, or their women, or what their right hands own...}* (24:31).

When early scholars asked why paternal and maternal uncles were not mentioned in these two Ayat, 'Ikrimah and Ash-Sha'bi explained that uncles were omitted because they might describe the woman's beauty to their sons (her eligible cousins), making it disliked for a woman to remove her veil before paternal and maternal uncles.

Regarding *{or their women}*, it means free believing women do not have to observe Hijab in front of other believing women.

Regarding *{or what their right (hands) own}*, **the majority position is that it means their slaves, both male and female, as established in the authentic Sunnah.** In contrast, Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib held: **"This means female slaves only."** (Recorded by Ibn Abi Hatim).

Allah concludes: *{But guard (yourselves) against God. Surely God is a witness over everything}*, commanding women to maintain God-fearing piety in secret and in public, mindful that Allah witnesses all things and nothing is hidden from Him.

tafsir_tabari.text:
### Exceptions to the Veil for the Prophet's Wives

Regarding the interpretation of the Word of the Exalted: **{(There is) no blame on them concerning their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons, or their women, or what their right (hands) own. But guard (yourselves) against God. Surely God is a witness over everything.}** (55)

He, exalted be His mention, says: There is no sin or fault upon the wives of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concerning their close male relatives, their women, or their slaves.

The scholars of interpretation differed regarding the nature of the exemption:
- Mujahid stated that it means permission to lay aside their outer cloaks (*jalabib*) in the presence of these individuals and to be seen by them.
- Qatadah stated: "He permitted for these relatives that the wives do not need to observe Hijab in front of them."

Imam al-Tabari concludes: **The closer of the two opinions to what is correct is that it means the lifting of the obligation of observing Hijab (curtain/veil) before these individuals.** This verse follows immediately after the general command of Hijab (*{And when you ask them for an item, ask them from behind a curtain}*), functioning as an explicit legal exemption from that universal restriction.

### Legal Categories: Relatives, Women, and Slaves

The legal meaning is: **There is no sin upon the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in giving permission to enter and leaving off the Hijab in front of their fathers, their sons, their brothers, and their brothers' sons.** The paternal and maternal uncles were not mentioned in the verse; Ash-Sha'bi and 'Ikrimah explained that this was out of caution lest they describe the women to their own sons, and they disliked that a woman should remove her head-covering (*khimar*) before her uncles.

Regarding His saying, **{or their women}**, He says: **There is no blame upon them in leaving off the Hijab in front of believing, free Muslim women.** Ibn Zayd explained: "The believing free women may look upon their adornment, but it is not permissible for a woman to look at any part of the private nakedness (*'awrah*) of another woman."

Regarding His saying, **{or what their right (hands) own}**, scholars differed: some held it refers to both male and female owned slaves, while others restricted it to female slaves.

Ibn Zayd explained the legal practice of the Prophet's household: **"The wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not observe Hijab in front of their owned slaves (*mamalik*)."** He noted that while a woman should not expose inner adornments such as earrings to male slaves, there is no harm in them seeing outward adornment such as eyeliner (*kuhl*), rings, and henna dye (*khidab*).

### Admonition and Divine Witness

Regarding His saying, **{But guard (yourselves) against God}**, He says: **Fear Allah, O women, lest you transgress the boundaries Allah has set for you by exposing adornment that is forbidden to reveal, or by abandoning the Hijab in front of anyone other than those whom He explicitly exempted.**

Regarding *{Surely God is a witness over everything}*, He says: Allah is fully witness over your observance or neglect of Hijab and all your deeds; so fear meeting Allah in disobedience to His explicit commands and prohibitions.

faqs.question: Did Islam seek to gradually abolish slavery?
faqs.apologetic_claim: Islam introduced a gradual abolition roadmap designed to phase out slavery over time through voluntary manumission and religious expiations.
faqs.short_answer: No. Canonical primary sources demonstrate that Islam never established a gradual abolition roadmap or sought to eliminate slavery. Neither the Quran nor Muhammad ever outlawed chattel slavery, set a timeline for its phaseout, or treated total emancipation as an ultimate legal objective.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Canonical primary sources demonstrate that Islam never established a gradual abolition roadmap or sought to extinguish slavery. Neither the Quran nor Muhammad ever prohibited the institution of chattel slavery, set a sunset date or timeline for its elimination, or treated total emancipation as an ultimate legal objective.

### Primary Canonical Evidence Refuting an Abolition Roadmap:
- **Active Human Trafficking and Slave Barter:** Muhammad regularly bought, sold, and captured slaves throughout his prophetic career, explicitly bartering two black slaves to purchase a single Muslim slave [[Sahih Muslim 22:152](https://sunnah.com/muslim/22/152)].
- **Revoking Freedom to Publicly Auction Slaves:** When a debtor stipulated posthumous emancipation (*tadbir*) for his slave, Muhammad intervened, cancelled the manumission, took physical possession of the Coptic slave, and publicly auctioned him to the highest bidder for 800 dirhams [[Sahih al-Bukhari 6716](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6716) / [Sahih Muslim 27:85](https://sunnah.com/muslim/27/85)].
- **Overriding Emancipation and Re-Enslavement via Lots:** When an Ansari man manumitted all six of his slaves upon his deathbed without leaving other assets, Muhammad revoked the full manumission, divided the six freed men into three pairs, cast lots to free only two, and legally remanded the remaining four back into permanent chattel slavery [[Sahih Muslim 27:78](https://sunnah.com/muslim/27/78)].
- **Rebuking Voluntary Manumission:** When Muhammad's wife Maymuna emancipated her female slave girl and informed him, Muhammad rebuked her decision, explicitly stating that she would have received a greater heavenly reward had she gifted the slave girl to her maternal uncles to keep in domestic servitude [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2592](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2592) / [Sahih Muslim 12:54](https://sunnah.com/muslim/12/54)].
- **Manumission Requires Slavery's Perpetuity:** Islamic law instituted slave freeing primarily as an expiation (*Kaffara*) for sins like broken oaths or involuntary manslaughter [[Qur'an 4:92](quran/4#92), [Sahih Muslim 13:103](https://sunnah.com/muslim/13/103)]; this structural mechanism *requires* the ongoing existence of a slave market in perpetuity so that future believers can buy slaves to atone for sins.
- **Lifelong Slave Ownership and Zero Prohibition:** No verse in the Quran and no sahih hadith ever outlaws slavery or instructs the Muslim community to phase it out; rather, Muhammad maintained personal slaves in his household until his death in 11 AH [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2739](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2739)].

faqs.question: Were slaves in Islam merely household servants or paid domestic workers?
faqs.apologetic_claim: Islamic slavery was not chattel slavery, but merely voluntary employment, domestic servanthood, or paid contract labor.
faqs.short_answer: No. Canonical primary sources establish that enslaved human beings were legally classified as disposable chattel property (māl), barter commodities, and financial currency that could be publicly auctioned for cash, traded in multi-person barter transactions, seized for debts, liquidated for misconduct, and assessed as blood-money indemnity.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Canonical primary sources establish that enslaved human beings were legally classified as disposable **chattel property (*māl*)**, **barter commodities**, and **financial currency**—not contractual wage earners:

### Primary Canonical Evidence of Chattel Status:
- **Public Cash Auctions for Debt:** When an Ansari man attempted to posthumously free his only slave while in debt, Muhammad cancelled the manumission (*tadbir*), seized physical custody of the slave, and publicly auctioned him to the highest bidder (*"Who will buy this slave from me?"*), selling him for 800 silver dirhams to Nu'aym ibn al-Nahham [[Sahih al-Bukhari 6716](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6716) / [Sahih Muslim 27:85](https://sunnah.com/muslim/27/85)].
- **Human Barter & Bulk Commodity Exchange:** Muhammad directly traded human beings as exchange commodities. When a runaway slave pledged allegiance without his owner's consent, Muhammad refused to release him and instead purchased the convert by bartering two enslaved black men in exchange for the single slave [[Sahih Muslim 22:152](https://sunnah.com/muslim/22/152)]. Similarly, to acquire Safiyya bint Huyayy from Dihya al-Kalbi following the fall of Khaybar, Muhammad compensated him with seven slave heads (*sab'at ar'us*) [[Sahih Muslim 16:99](https://sunnah.com/muslim/16/99)].
- **Mandated Forced Liquidation on the Slave Market:** Rather than terminating an employment contract, Muhammad legally legislated that if an unmarried female slave (*amah*) commits illegal sexual intercourse repeatedly, her master must flog her without verbal rebuke and then forcibly liquidate her on the open slave market even for the paltry price of a braided hair rope [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2555](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2555) / [Sahih Muslim 29:38](https://sunnah.com/muslim/29/38)].
- **Slaves as Statutory Blood-Money Currency (*Ghurrah*):** Under Islamic criminal law, human slave bodies functioned as standardized legal tender; Muhammad legislated that the statutory blood-money indemnity (*ghurrah*) for causing a pregnant woman to miscarry a dead fetus is the surrender of a male or female slave [[Sahih al-Bukhari 5758](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5758) / [Sahih Muslim 28:48](https://sunnah.com/muslim/28/48)].
- **Master Expropriation of Slave Earnings (*Kharaj*):** Enslaved individuals had no independent legal right to retain their wages; when the slave cupper Abu Tayba performed medical cupping for Muhammad, Muhammad paid him a wage but had to personally negotiate with Abu Tayba's masters to reduce the daily tax/tribute (*kharaj / daribah*) they routinely extorted from their slave's labor [[Sahih Muslim 22:81](https://sunnah.com/muslim/22/81)].

faqs.question: Were Safiyya, Juwayriyya, and Maria al-Qibtiyya honored, consensual wives rather than war captives or concubines?
faqs.apologetic_claim: These women freely chose marriage with Muhammad to elevate their social standing rather than being subjugated as captive war booty (ghanīma / sabī) or slave concubines (milk al-yamīn).
faqs.short_answer: No. Canonical historical and hadith records document their direct subjugation through military capture, family executions, coerced dowry arrangements, and unfree concubinage.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Canonical historical and hadith records document their direct subjugation through military capture, coerced dowry arrangements, and concubinage:

### Primary Canonical Evidence on Captive Consorts:
- **Safiyya bint Huyayy (War Captive Bartered for 7 Slaves & Dowry Coercion):**
  - **Husband & Father Slain:** Her father Huyayy ibn Akhtab was executed following the Banu Qurayza siege [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4121](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4121) / [Sahih Muslim 32:64](https://sunnah.com/muslim/32/64)], and her husband Kinana ibn al-Rabi' was executed during the Khaybar campaign [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4200](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4200) / [Sahih Muslim 16:96](https://sunnah.com/muslim/16/96)], where Safiyya was seized as captive booty (*al-saby*) [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4200](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4200)].
  - **Bartered for 7 Slave Heads:** Companion Dihya al-Kalbi initially chose her from the captives; when companions protested that a noble chieftain's daughter should belong only to Muhammad, Muhammad retrieved her and compensated Dihya with seven slave heads (*sab'ata ar'us*) [[Sahih Muslim 16:99](https://sunnah.com/muslim/16/99)].
  - **Manumission Retained as Dowry:** Her legal manumission (*'itq*) was withheld and made her compulsory bridal dowry (*mahr* / *sadaq*), giving her no choice of freedom independent of marrying Muhammad [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4200](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4200) / [Sahih Muslim 16:96](https://sunnah.com/muslim/16/96) / [Sahih al-Bukhari 5086](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5086)].
  - **Sahaba's Veil Test (Wife vs. Concubine):** Companions could not determine whether she was a free wife or an unmanumitted right-hand slave concubine (*milk al-yamin*), declaring: *"If he veils her, she is one of the Mothers of the Believers; and if he does not veil her, she is from what his right hand possesses"* [[Sahih al-Bukhari 5387](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5387) / [Sahih al-Bukhari 4201](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4201)].
  - **Immediate Roadside Consummation:** Muhammad pitched a bridal tent and consummated the union at al-Sahba' on the march back to Medina within days of her family's execution [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4200](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4200) / [Sahih Muslim 16:99](https://sunnah.com/muslim/16/99)].
- **Juwayriyya bint al-Harith (Enslaved Spoils of a Surprise Dawn Raid):**
  - **Surprise Dawn Raid & Tribal Enslavement:** Muhammad assaulted Banu al-Mustaliq without warning while their cattle were drinking, killing fighting men and taking women and children as enslaved captives (*sabā dharāriyyahum*) [[Sahih Muslim 32:1](https://sunnah.com/muslim/32/1) / [Sahih al-Bukhari 2541](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2541)].
  - **Distributed as Booty & Ransomed:** Assigned as war booty to Thabit ibn Qays; she negotiated a contract of emancipation (*kitaba*), which Muhammad purchased in exchange for taking her into his household [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2541](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2541)].
- **Maria al-Qibtiyya (Enslaved Gift & Lifelong Right-Hand Concubine):**
  - **Gifted Slave Concubine:** Sent as an enslaved concubine (*jariyah*) by the Muqawqis of Egypt; she was never married through a *nikah* contract, was retained strictly under right-hand possession (*Milk al-Yamin*) [[Sunan an-Nasa'i 3959](https://sunnah.com/nasai:3959)], and remained enslaved until Muhammad's death [[Sunan Ibn Majah 2516](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:2516)].

faqs.question: Was sexual intercourse with female captives (Milk al-Yamin) prohibited without formal marriage?
faqs.apologetic_claim: Masters were forbidden from having sexual intercourse with female captives or slave concubines unless they first freed and legally married them.
faqs.short_answer: No. Islamic scripture and jurisprudence explicitly establish that Milk al-Yamīn (property ownership) is an independent legal basis for sexual relations requiring no marriage contract (nikāḥ), no dowry, and no female consent.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Islamic scripture and jurisprudence explicitly establish that **Milk al-Yamīn** (property ownership) is an independent legal basis for sexual relations requiring no marriage contract (*nikāḥ*), no dowry, and no female consent:

### Primary Canonical Evidence for Slave Concubinage:
- **Qur'anic Separation of Wives and Concubines:** The Qur'an systematically defines lawful sexual intercourse as restricted to two distinct, mutually exclusive legal categories: free wives (*azwājihim*) **OR** right-hand slave possessions (*mā malakat aymānuhum*) [[Qur'an 23:5–6](quran/23#5-6), [Qur'an 70:29–30](quran/70#29-30)].
- **Sanctioning Sex with Married Captives ([Qur'an 4:24](quran/4#24)):** Revealed at Awtas when Muslim soldiers hesitated to sleep with captured women whose pagan husbands were still alive; Allah sanctioned intercourse with them by dissolving their marriages upon capture [[Sahih Muslim 17:41](https://sunnah.com/muslim/17/41), [Sahih Muslim 17:43](https://sunnah.com/muslim/17/43)].
- **Coitus Interruptus (*'Azl*) to Protect Slave Market Value:** Muslim warriors took captive Arab women at Banu al-Mustaliq, desired sexual gratification, and practiced coitus interruptus (*'azl*) to avoid pregnancies that would prevent selling them for ransom on the slave market; Muhammad explicitly permitted the practice [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4138](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4138) / [Sahih Muslim 16:146](https://sunnah.com/muslim/16/146), [Sahih al-Bukhari 5210](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5210)].
- **Ali Taking a Khums Slave-Girl for Sex:** Ali had sexual intercourse with an unmarried captive girl from the state fifth (*Khums*) in Yemen without marriage; when Burayda complained, Muhammad defended Ali, declaring he was entitled to even more female slaves from the Khums [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4350](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4350), [Sahih al-Bukhari 7374](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7374)].
- **Aisha's Testimony on Milk al-Yamin:** Aisha confirmed that Muhammad's sexual contact was strictly limited to his wives and the women possessed by his right hand [[Sahih al-Bukhari 7214](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7214)].

faqs.question: Did Muhammad personally own, buy, sell, or trade slaves?
faqs.apologetic_claim: Muhammad never personally owned, bought, sold, or bartered slaves, but only inherited or emancipated them.
faqs.short_answer: No. Canonical primary sources document Muhammad's extensive personal slave ownership and active commercial slave trading, including public auctions, bartering 2-for-1, and household slave retainers.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Canonical primary sources document Muhammad's extensive personal slave ownership of active chattel slaves and his participation in commercial slave trading:

### Primary Canonical Evidence on Personal Slaves & Trading:
- **Named Personal Slaves of Muhammad (Active Chattel):**
  - **Mid'am:** Personal black slave boy gifted to Muhammad by Rifa'a bin Zaid, tending saddles and luggage at Wadi al-Qura [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4234](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4234) / [Sahih Muslim 1:217](https://sunnah.com/muslim/1:217)].
  - **Rabah:** Personal black slave boy and private chamber doorkeeper [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4913](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4913) / [Sahih Muslim 18:40](https://sunnah.com/muslim/18/40)].
  - **Karkara:** Personal slave in charge of managing Muhammad's travel baggage and belongings [[Sahih al-Bukhari 3074](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3074)].
  - **Anjasha:** Personal black slave camel-driver and chanter [[Sahih al-Bukhari 6149](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6149) / [Sahih Muslim 43:94](https://sunnah.com/muslim/43/94)].
  - **Personal Slave Craftsmen & Domestic Servants:** Enslaved carpenter commanded to construct Muhammad's mosque pulpit [[Sahih al-Bukhari 917](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:917) / [Sahih Muslim 5:33](https://sunnah.com/muslim/5:33)], and an Abyssinian domestic maidservant who prepared steeped drinks in his household [[Sahih Muslim 36:105](https://sunnah.com/muslim/36/105)].
  - **The Flogged Household Slave-Girl:** Female slave belonging to Allah's Messenger who committed adultery and whom Muhammad ordered Ali to flog [[Sahih Muslim 29:53](https://sunnah.com/muslim/29/53)].
- **Direct Commercial Transactions:** Bartered two black slaves to purchase one Muslim slave [[Sahih Muslim 22:152](https://sunnah.com/muslim/22/152)], purchased Safiyya from Dihya for seven slave heads [[Sahih Muslim 16:99](https://sunnah.com/muslim/16/99)], and publicly auctioned the mudabbar slave for 800 dirhams [[Sahih al-Bukhari 6716](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6716)].

faqs.question: Was enslavement in Islam strictly limited to aggressive enemy combatants?
faqs.apologetic_claim: Enslavement was purely a defensive wartime measure restricted exclusively to aggressive enemy soldiers captured on the battlefield.
faqs.short_answer: No. Male combatants were routinely executed or held as prisoners; enslavement was overwhelmingly and systematically targeted at civilian non-combatants—specifically innocent women, nursing mothers, young boys, and children.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Male combatants were routinely executed or held as prisoners of war; enslavement was systematically targeted at non-combatant civilian women and children:

### Primary Canonical Evidence on Civilian Enslavement:
- **Mass Enslavement at Banu Qurayza:** Following the siege of the Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayza, Sa'd bin Mu'adh decreed that all fighting men be executed while all non-combatant civilian women and children be seized and enslaved as war spoils, a ruling Muhammad explicitly ratified as Allah's divine decree from above the seven heavens [[Sahih al-Bukhari 4121](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4121) / [Sahih Muslim 32:64](https://sunnah.com/muslim/32/64)].
- **6,000 Captive Women and Children of Hawazin:** After defeating the Hawazin at the Battle of Hunayn, Muhammad and his army captured approximately 6,000 non-combatant women and children, who were systematically inventoried as war spoils (*ghanima*) and distributed among the Muslim soldiers as slaves and concubines [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2583](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2583) / [Sahih al-Bukhari 4318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4318)].
- **Surprise Dawn Raid on Banu al-Mustaliq Civilians:** Muhammad commanded an unprovoked surprise dawn assault on the unsuspecting tribe of Banu al-Mustaliq while they were heedless and their cattle were drinking at the watering stations, killing their men who resisted and taking all civilian women and children into captivity as chattel slaves [[Sahih Muslim 32:1](https://sunnah.com/muslim/32/1) / [Sahih al-Bukhari 2541](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2541)].
- **Immediate Sexual Utilization of Captured Civilian Women:** Following raids on tribes like Banu al-Mustaliq and Hawazin (at Awtas), the captured civilian women—whose existing marriages were instantly dissolved upon capture—were immediately distributed as sex slaves to Muslim warriors who practiced coitus interruptus (*'azl*) with them [[Sahih Muslim 17:41](https://sunnah.com/muslim/17/41) / [Sahih al-Bukhari 2542](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2542)].

faqs.question: Did Islam grant slaves equal legal and human rights to free Muslims?
faqs.apologetic_claim: Islam established complete legal, civil, and religious equality between enslaved persons and free Muslims.
faqs.short_answer: No. Classical Islamic jurisprudence codified slaves as a subordinate legal caste with severely diminished civil rights, unequal criminal penalties, and diminished modesty boundaries.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Classical Islamic law codified slaves as a subordinate caste with severely diminished legal and civil rights:

### Primary Legal & Jurisprudential Asymmetries:
- **Runaway Slaves Classified as Infidels (*Kufr*):** Enslaved individuals who fled their masters were legally classified as apostates/infidels (*kāfir*) whose prayers were rejected by Allah and whose covenant of protection was annulled until they returned to servitude [[Sahih Muslim 1:134](https://sunnah.com/muslim/1/134)].
- **Exclusion from Combat Booty Shares:** Enslaved men who participated in military expeditions were legally denied the statutory fixed shares of war spoils (*sahm*) granted to free Muslim soldiers, receiving only minor discretionary leftovers (*radkh*) [[Sahih Muslim 32:166](https://sunnah.com/muslim/32/166)].
- **Slaves Codified as Standard Blood-Money Currency (*Ghurrah*):** Muhammad codified human slaves as commercial property units used as statutory currency for paying fetal blood-money (*ghurrah*) upon the termination of a pregnancy [[Sahih al-Bukhari 5758](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5758) / [Sahih Muslim 28:48](https://sunnah.com/muslim/28/48)].
- **Adultery Penalties & Mandatory Liquidation:** When an unmarried enslaved woman committed adultery, her master was commanded to flog her with 50 lashes and, upon repeated offenses, mandated her forced sale on the commercial market even for a meager braided hair rope [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2555](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2555) / [Sahih Muslim 29:38](https://sunnah.com/muslim/29/38)].
- **Perpetual Master Monopoly Over Patronal Inheritance (*Walā'*):** Muhammad established that patronal inheritance rights (*walā'*) belong exclusively and irrevocably to the purchasing master who manumits the slave, strictly voiding any private contractual stipulations to the contrary [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2560](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2560) / [Sahih Muslim 20:7](https://sunnah.com/muslim/20/7)].
- **Compulsory Theological Tests for Manumission:** Masters were not permitted to emancipate slaves for religious expiation without undergoing mandatory theological interrogation by Muhammad to verify their creedal orthodoxy [[Sahih Muslim 5:33](https://sunnah.com/muslim/5/33)].

faqs.question: Why did Islam encourage freeing slaves (Manumission / 'Itq) if it did not intend to abolish slavery?
faqs.apologetic_claim: The numerous Islamic texts encouraging slave manumission (freeing slaves) prove that Islam aimed for the total abolition of slavery.
faqs.short_answer: Encouraging individual manumission ('Itq)—especially as sin expiation (Kaffara)—presupposes and requires the perpetual continuation of slavery. An economic system that uses slaves as fine currency cannot function if slavery is abolished.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**No.** Conflating individual pious manumission (*'Itq*) with structural legal abolition is a fundamental theological error. Islamic law actively structured slave manumission in a manner that **necessitates the perpetual continuation of slavery**:

### Why Manumission Does Not Equal Abolition:
- **Slaves as Sin Currency (*Kaffara*):** Islamic law instituted slave freeing primarily as an expiation/fine (*Kaffara*) for religious offenses, including breaking oaths [[Qur'an 5:89](quran/5#89)], accidental manslaughter [[Qur'an 4:92](quran/4#92)], breaking the Ramadan fast [[Sahih Muslim 13:103](https://sunnah.com/muslim/13/103)], and marital zihar oaths [[Qur'an 58:3](quran/58#3)].
- **The Kaffara Paradox:** You cannot pay a statutory fine with a commodity that does not exist. If slavery were abolished, believers would be completely incapable of fulfilling divine Kaffara mandates. The Sharia therefore requires an ongoing, permanent supply of enslaved human beings (via ongoing military Jihad and hereditary slave births) for future generations of sinners to purchase and free.
- **Overriding Emancipation to Protect Estate Wealth:** When individual manumission threatened economic stability or debt settlement, Muhammad actively intervened to cancel freedom. When a dying man freed his six slaves, Muhammad revoked the manumission, drew lots to keep four in slavery, and cursed the deceased owner [[Sahih Muslim 27:78](https://sunnah.com/muslim/27/78)].
- **Prioritizing Domestic Servitude over Freedom:** When Maymuna freed a slave-girl, Muhammad rebuked her, declaring she would have gained more heavenly reward had she gifted the girl to her relatives to keep as a domestic servant [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2592](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2592) / [Sahih Muslim 12:54](https://sunnah.com/muslim/12/54)].
- **Zero Abolition Mandate:** While classical Sharia classified manumission as supererogatory (*mustahabb* / recommended), it classified the institution of slavery as permanent, permissible, and divinely sanctioned until the Day of Judgment.

faqs.question: What were the major Fiqh (Jurisprudential) asymmetries between slaves and free Muslims in classical Islamic Law?
faqs.apologetic_claim: Under classical Sharia (Fiqh), slaves possessed equal human dignity, identical modesty standards, and equal legal protection under criminal law.
faqs.short_answer: Classical Fiqh institutionalized severe legal asymmetries: female slaves had a diminished 'awrah and were forbidden/discouraged from wearing the hijab; free Muslims were exempt from capital retaliation (Qisas) for killing slaves; and slaves received half-punishments and had zero independent property capacity.
faqs.answer_markdown:
**Classical Islamic Law (Fiqh) codified profound, institutionalized asymmetries between enslaved persons and free Muslims:**

### 1. The Awrah & Hijab Asymmetry (The Veil Test):
- **The Hijab as a Marker of Free Status:** In classical Fiqh, the hijab was an exclusive legal badge of free women (*hurra*), not slave women (*amah*). Female slaves had a significantly reduced *'awrah* (intimate area), generally defined by jurists (including the Hanafi, Maliki, and Hanbali schools) as similar to a man (navel to knee) or allowing the chest, arms, and hair to remain uncovered during domestic labor.
- **The Sahaba's Veil Test:** When Muhammad captured Safiyya bint Huyayy at Khaybar, the Companions determined her legal status entirely by whether she was veiled: *"If he veils her, she is one of the Mothers of the Believers (a free wife); and if he does not veil her, she is from what his right hand possesses (an unmanumitted slave concubine)"* [[Sahih al-Bukhari 5387](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5387)].
- **Caliph Umar's Prohibition on Slaves Veiling:** Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab famously struck an enslaved woman who had covered herself with a veil, commanding her: *"Do not resemble free women!"* (*Sunan al-Kubra al-Bayhaqi 3279*, *Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah 6236*).

### 2. Criminal & Penal Asymmetries (Qisas & Hadd):
- **Exemption from Capital Retaliation (*Qisas*):** Under the majority consensus of classical Sunni Fiqh (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali), a free Muslim is not subjected to capital execution (*Qisas*) for murdering an enslaved person, because slaves are property (*mal*) whose blood-value is not equal to a free person.
- **Halved Penalties for Slaves:** Under [Qur'an 4:25](quran/4#25), an enslaved woman convicted of adultery receives **half the punishment** of a free unmarried woman (50 lashes instead of 100) and cannot be stoned to death, reflecting her halved legal accountability and diminished social personhood [[Sahih al-Bukhari 2555](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2555)].

### 3. Civil, Marital & Property Incapacity:
- **Zero Independent Property Rights:** The Qur'an defines an owned slave as having *"no power over anything"* [[Qur'an 16:75](quran/16#75)]; all property or earnings acquired by a slave belong legally to the master [[Sahih Muslim 22:81](https://sunnah.com/muslim/22/81)].
- **No Autonomous Marriage Rights:** A slave cannot contract a marriage without the master's express legal consent; any marriage contracted independently is legally null and void, and the slave is deemed a fornicator [[Qur'an 4:25](quran/4#25), *Sunan Abi Dawud 2078*].
